Scope of record: docs/plans/OPERATING-PLAN-2026-09-21.md. Manager contract: .claude/skills/manager/SKILL.md.
The previous 323-row file is preserved verbatim at
RULES FOR THIS FILE, because the last one grew 67 top-level keys and 323 rows:
1. items[] is the content. Top-level keys are schema only - no narrative,
no timestamped manager_observation_* / manager_tick_* entries, no incident logs.
Three observations an hour apart on one row is the failure mode, not diligence.
2. ONE status field: `state`, from the `states` vocabulary below. There is no `status`.
3. `done` and `landed_unproven` are DIFFERENT FACTS and are never collapsed.
4. A row that is neither a plan item nor a live lane does not belong here.
A question goes to research/queue/<id>.yaml instead.
5. This file is served to the operator as the live Workflow page via
GET /api/bot/work/checklist, read from the VM's working tree. ict-git-sync
pulls main every ~5 min, so the page is as fresh as the last push TO MAIN.

last_review._comment: Set by the manager's daily review (manager SKILL § 'The work system'): the WR-YYYYMMDD-HHMMZ report it worked from GET /api/bot/work/report, when, by whom, and disposition counts. Per-item dispositions live on the pipeline items. null = no review recorded yet.

cycle_intent: Make the promotion ladder mechanical and the research loop terminate in a decision. Edge is decided offline; a book only ever checks mechanics and cost.

priorities.decided: operator, AskUserQuestion popup in manager session_01KAQRJxRbRwpYTkPgBjNVyQ, 2026-09-28 ~08:55Z, verbatim answer "Prop first (Recommended)"
priorities.floor: anything broken on a live-money or prop money path jumps the queue, whatever its theme
order: 1 Prop account — roster (candidates ONLY from https://www.breakoutprop.com/symbols/), sizing, exits
5 Macro sleeve (M28 re-shape via research; M29 dormant until it reads out)
priorities.how_used: Lanes are assigned top-down; the research queue is weighted ~30/25/20/15/10 in this order; Fable goes to the highest-value research items at the manager's discretion (operator 2026-09-28: most Fable budget to high-value research, not every research task). Operator decisions surface as popups ranked by this order.

states.queued: scoped and agreed, nobody started it
states.in_flight: a lane is actively working it
states.blocked: waiting on the typed edge(s) in blocked_on
states.dropped: deliberately not doing; note says why

item_schema.id: plan item id (A1..D3) or a lane id
item_schema.title: one line
item_schema.lane: session id once dispatched, else null
item_schema.model: the model chosen for the lane, with the reason in `note`
item_schema.ceiling_usd: per-lane dollar ceiling; on breach READ what it produced, then kill or re-scope
item_schema.spend_usd: actual, filled in by the cost meter (A1)
item_schema.tier: 1 | 2 | 3 - the approval the resulting change needs
item_schema.blocked_on: typed edges [{kind, ref, what}] — kind is `work_item` or `operator_decision`, ref names the blocker, what says why. Empty list = nothing declared blocks it.
item_schema.note: what is true about this row. Not a log.

items.title: Cost meter — usage against the WEEKLY PLAN ALLOWANCE, plus per-lane dollars
items.note: OPERATOR DECISION 2026-09-21: 'pace ourselves based on the weekly budget for the $200 Max plan -- 10% of the weekly budget a day, so we leave a wide margin for error or unexpected needs.' 10%/day x 7 = 70% of the weekly allowance, 30% margin. [!] THIS CHANGES WHAT THIS ITEM MEASURES AND THE CHANGE IS NOT COSMETIC. A subscription plan's constraint is a WEEKLY USAGE ALLOWANCE, not a dollar spend. Every cost_usd figure in the plan (the $125 across two resumed lanes, the $11.88 in ten minutes) is API-EQUIVALENT PRICING read off session metadata -- the right signal for COMPARING lanes, the wrong denominator for PACING against a plan. Report usage-against-allowance as the budget line, keep dollars beside it as the per-lane comparison. [!] THE DENOMINATOR IS NOT ESTABLISHED AND MUST NOT BE INVENTED: the exact weekly allowance is not readable from this repo. FIRST JOB is to establish it from whatever surface reports plan usage, or from the operator, and to report `unknown` rather than substitute a figure until it has. A fabricated denominator under a real rule is worse than no meter. [!] THE DENOMINATOR IS ESTABLISHED 2026-09-21, AND IT IS A PERCENTAGE, NOT A TOKEN COUNT. The operator read Settings > Usage directly. Plan: Max (20x). The surface exposes THREE meters, each a percent-of-allowance bar with no absolute number anywhere: a ~5-hour SESSION window, a WEEKLY window, and a SEPARATE WEEKLY LIMIT FOR FABLE. Anthropic's own support pages publish no figure either -- only '20x Pro per-session allowance'. [!] DO NOT CONVERT TO TOKENS, and this is a design decision rather than a limitation. The allowance is MODEL-WEIGHTED, so tokens-per-percent is not a constant -- it is a function of the model mix and moves whenever the manager routes a lane to sonnet instead of opus. A token budget would read as precise and drift silently. A1 METERS IN PERCENT. The operator's rule -- 10% of the weekly budget per day -- is already stated in that unit, so no conversion is needed to enforce it. A measured per-model exchange rate may be reported as a sanity check, labelled measured and drifting, NEVER as the budget. [!] TWO WINDOWS BIND, NOT ONE. The weekly cap is what the 10%/day rule governs; the ~5-hour session window is what actually walls a lane mid-run. A day's 10% spent as a single burst can exhaust the session window while the weekly meter still reads green, so A1 MUST SHOW BOTH or it reports 'fine' during an outage. [!] MEASURED 2026-09-21, and it CORRECTS an earlier claim on this row that was asserted rather than checked. The claim was that a meter summing only agent lanes would systematically under-report because the operator's own chat draws on the same pool. The mechanism is real -- all surfaces do share one limit -- but the magnitude is currently ZERO: 'What's using your week' reads Claude Code 100%, Chats 0%, Cowork 0%, Other 0%. Lane accounting is therefore ~= the whole pool today. A1 should still LABEL its scope, because the day that mix changes the meter goes quietly wrong. [!] THE MANAGER'S METER IS THE **DAILY** BUDGET, NOT THE WEEKLY BAR (operator, 2026-09-21): 'the manager should be focused on the daily budget, not weekly, as I sometimes use Claude for other projects... I will start a new manager session after this one and I expect it to use the daily budget, even if we pass into the margin.' [!] THIS CORRECTS A CLAIM WRITTEN ON THIS ROW EARLIER THE SAME DAY, and it is the SAME CATEGORY ERROR this row already caught once with cost_usd. That claim read: '68% of the week consumed with ~2 of 7 days left, ~13.6%/day against a 10%/day target, so THE STATED POLICY IS NOT BEING MET.' It compared TOTAL weekly consumption against the MANAGER'S daily allowance -- two different populations. The weekly bar aggregates every surface and every project the operator touches, including work this repo's manager cannot see and did not cause, so it CANNOT grade the manager. ('Claude Code 100%' does not rescue it: the operator's other projects are also Claude Code.) The 68% reading stands as a fact about the ACCOUNT; the conclusion drawn from it was unsupported and is withdrawn. [!] SO A1 REPORTS TWO DIFFERENT THINGS AND MUST NOT BLEND THEM. (a) THE CONTROL VARIABLE: this repo's spend today against the daily budget -- 10% of the weekly allowance. That is the number the manager is accountable for. (b) CONTEXT ONLY: the account-level weekly bar, unattributable and reported as such. A single blended 'budget' figure is the bug. [!] THE 30% WEEKLY MARGIN IS NOT A RESERVE THE MANAGER PRESERVES BY DOING LESS. It exists to absorb the operator's other projects and surprises. A manager that throttles its own lane because the ACCOUNT bar looks high is spending the margin's purpose on nothing. The operator has stated explicitly that the next manager should spend its daily budget EVEN IF that passes into the margin. [!] AND THE FAILURE MODE IS NOT HITTING A CAP -- it is 'losing work to sessions dying in the middle' (operator). THAT IS A DURABILITY PROBLEM, NOT A BUDGET ONE, and budgeting alone cannot fix it. The mitigations are structural: land work in small PRs rather than one large one, push before you answer, and keep state on disk (PIPELINE.jsonl, the checklist) rather than in a session's head. The ~5-HOUR SESSION WINDOW is what actually kills a session mid-task, so it is the in-session number to watch; the weekly bar never killed anything mid-run. [!] FABLE HAS A SEPARATE WEEKLY ALLOWANCE, MEASURED AT 0% USED, AND THE OPERATOR HAS DIRECTED THAT IT BE EMPLOYED (2026-09-21): 'it should definitely be used when appropriate -- we want to employ that budget as well, we just want to make sure it is getting the tasks that are the best use of that resource.' It is a SECOND pool that does not draw on the main one, so work routed there is additive capacity, not a trade-off. That makes it a live routing input for the model table in .claude/skills/manager/SKILL.md. Tracked as E11 -- A1 reports the pool, E11 decides what goes in it. [!] DISPATCHED 2026-09-21 alongside A3a rather than before it, because A3a was told to render section 5 WITHOUT the spend figures (it already has the unrouted count from pipeline.py) and to print an explicit 'not measured -- A1 not built' line. So the blocked_on edge is narrower than it read: section 5 ships either way and A1 fills it in. FRESH, sonnet-5. [!] THE QUESTION PUT TO THE LANE is deliberately not 'build a cost meter' but 'what does section 5 print on a day nobody has read the usage meter' -- because the denominator is not machine-readable and the failure mode on this row has twice been a figure that looked precise and was not. [!] BUILT 2026-09-21, PR #12683 open (draft, not merged -- state stays `in_flight` until the manager merges it; move to `landed_unproven` on merge, and `done` only once A3a's section-5 wiring is observed calling this module in a real brief): `scripts/ops/spend_meter.py` -- an append-only on-disk record of operator-entered readings (session/weekly/fable_weekly, percent + read_at) and `render_section_5()` for A3a to call. Verified this session: a day with no reading prints `never recorded` per window (never `0%`); a stale reading always renders its age and is never presented as current; per-lane `cost_usd` is reachable only from an interactive session holding `get_session`/`list_sessions` -- confirmed by calling those tools directly against this session and its parent manager -- and NOT from a CI runner or a Routine-fired turn (reconfirms, does not re-derive, the same finding already in `render_daily_brief.py` and `queue_latency.py`); no CI-reachable credential for it exists in this repo (checked: `.github/workflows/`, `docs/reference/env-vars.md`, `docs/claude/system-actions.md`). NOT yet wired into the real daily brief -- that is A3a's job, out of this row's scope fence. [!] MERGED 2026-09-21 as 9e9fb3a. ⚠️ SPEND CORRECTED 6.86 -> 28.03: the earlier figure was read MID-FLIGHT and left on the row looking like a total. A meter's own row reporting a stale number is the failure the meter exists to prevent. [!] ⚠️ SPEND CORRECTED AGAIN, READ AFTER ARCHIVING: $59.17. The figure committed hours earlier was ALSO mid-flight. [!] ⚠️ STATE CORRECTED BY THE LANE, NOT BY THE MANAGER (#12698): this row was marked `done` on the strength of #12683 merging, and the lane read origin/main:scripts/ops/render_daily_brief.py directly and found §5 STILL PRINTING `A1 (cost meter) is not built`. The meter is built, tested, guard-registered -- and nothing calls it. Merged is not deployed is not observed, and this row had collapsed the first into the third on the manager's say-so. [!] CLOSING THIS ROW MEANS: a real daily brief whose §5 prints a spend figure sourced from `spend_meter.render_section_5` -- not the placeholder `A1 (cost meter) is not built`, and not a hand-run of the module. The wiring is in `render_daily_brief.py`; re-reading `spend_meter.py` proves nothing, because the module was never the gap. RE-VERIFIED 2026-09-25: section 5 of GET /api/bot/work/brief still prints the literal placeholder "A1 (cost meter) is not built" (checked live, as_of/generatedAt 2026-09-25T13:25:07Z), and render_daily_brief.py has had zero commits since #12682 created it -- the wiring this row needs has not been attempted. Re-check: curl -sS https://ict-bot.duckdns.org/api/bot/work/brief; closes the day that string is replaced by a real spend_meter.render_section_5() figure.

SO B1 MUST KEY ON ROSTER MEMBERSHIP, not on the mode/execution fields: a guard watching only the fields can be walked around by editing the list, in either direction. This also matters for the mandates -- MD-PROMOTE-S1-S2 adds a leg to a roster, which is exactly the edit the current guard cannot see. [!] OPERATOR DECIDED THE BAR 2026-09-21: THE FOUR CLAUSES AS WRITTEN — named harness · stated n · net of the FULL cost stack · clearing a rule registered BEFORE the run. They were offered a fifth clause (an explicit minimum n, prompted by tlt_pullback_1d having reached a real-money roster on n=8) and declined it. [!] DISPATCHED 2026-09-21 on OPUS, not sonnet, and the reason is the task table's own rule rather than a preference: this guard decides what may reach a REAL-MONEY ROSTER. [!] LANE FENCED HARD out of changing any roster, mode or execution VALUE — it builds the guard only. If the guard fails current main, that is a FINDING TO REPORT, not a licence to edit config. [!] TOLD the minimum-n clause was OFFERED AND DECLINED, so it does not re-add one and does not read its absence as a gap. items.title: Cost fidelity as the standing Gate-1 test
items.note:
Is realized slippage what the harness assumed, per leg? This is what makes the ladder traversable for SLOW legs: a 1d leg can never establish expectancy on paper in usable time (23 of 52 legs are unbounded_no_closes), but cost fidelity converges in a handful of trades because it measures a per-trade quantity. Divergence demotes the leg AND invalidates its Stage-0 record, because the backtest assumed a cost the venue does not charge. Same unit as D3. items.title: Decide whether the system should trade at all right now
items.note: Asked explicitly rather than assumed. Lifetime real-money expectancy is -0.3231R over n=431. If R1 demotes most of the fleet the live books may be near-empty for a period. THAT IS AN ACCEPTABLE OUTCOME, not a failure -- the operator's own principle is that only proven-edge strategies run. No leg is kept live to avoid an empty roster. [!] OPERATOR DECIDED 2026-09-21: KEEP THE ROSTER AS-IS, DECIDE AFTER D1/R1. Asked as one of four popup decisions with the measurement stated (lifetime real-money expectancy -0.3231R over n=431, against a fee-only corpus optimistic by an unknown amount). They chose to hold current exposure rather than derisk now or pause real money. [!] THIS IS A DEFERRAL, NOT A CLOSURE, and deferrals are the class that gets silently settled — so it is ALSO filed as PI-20260921-M08 with a due condition tied to R1 landing, rather than left as a sentence here. The question comes BACK; it was not answered away. [!] THE STANDING derisk_only MANDATES ARE UNAFFECTED — they read live measurement rather than the corpus and are explicitly NOT blocked by D1, so a leg going net-negative on the mirror can still be pulled without re-asking. [!] KILLED 2026-09-22 ON OPERATOR INSTRUCTION, with the reason stated because a row that stops being mentioned instead of ending is the failure the pipeline rules name. Asked directly whether to dispatch a lane to build the decision packet, answer it in chat, or kill it, the operator chose KILL. TERMINAL REASON: this is not a decision anyone will ever take. The Prime Directive is that the trader runs 24/7 and never switches itself off — no auto-flip, no breaker that toggles mode, no safety default that goes dry on boot — and what trades is decided leg by leg through the two execution gates, on evidence, with demotion as the mechanism. A standing 'should the system trade at all' row has no decision procedure behind it and no evidence that would resolve it; it was a mood, not a question. If the real question ever returns it will arrive as a SPECIFIC demotion or an account-mode flip, which are Tier-3 and have their own path. ⚠️ THIS KILL IS NOT A JUDGEMENT THAT EVERYTHING IS FINE — E30 (the paper books' P&L is mostly unmeasured) and R8/E39 (which legs clear the bar) are the rows that carry the real content, and both are open.

items.title: Retire what the reset orphaned
items.note: 67 guard scripts unreachable from run_guards.py, kept because 30+ live files still name their paths. Right call today, poor steady state. One bounded pass: delete with references, or record why it stays. NOT by bulk deletion -- the reference sweep IS the job. [!] SCOPE CORRECTED 2026-09-21: THE GUARD SCRIPTS WERE NOT THE ONLY ORPHAN, and the pattern is worth more than the list. The reset disarmed every workflow that WRITES to a retired register and swept none of the ones that READ one. A writer to a missing register fails loudly; a reader degrades to 'could not check' and keeps issuing advice about a file that is gone. Two were found the same day: (a) scope-overlap-audit.yml, which posted 'read the coordination board yourself' on the reset's own PR and is DISARMED in this pass; (b) scripts/ops/render_daily_brief.py + its test, five of whose six inputs were archived and whose guard (daily-brief-guard) was dropped in the same pass -- NOT deleted here, because A3 replaces it and removing a renderer before its replacement exists is how a capability goes missing quietly. [!] THE SWEEP THIS ROW OWES IS THEREFORE A READER SWEEP, not a deletion pass: for each path under docs/archive/2026-09-21-operating-reset/, find what still reads it. A grep for the archived FILENAMES across .github/ and scripts/ is the probe, and it needs a positive control -- the two above are it. [!] SCOPE WIDENED AGAIN 2026-09-21, and this one was found by the OPERATOR LOOKING AT THE PAGE rather than by my sweep -- which is the finding about the sweep. I scoped the reader hunt to .github/ and scripts/ and never looked at src/web/api/, so THE API THAT SERVES THE WORKFLOW PAGE still reads three archived registers and says so to the operator on every load: (a) a 'Live work sessions' panel reading docs/claude/work/SESSIONS.json, which degrades honestly to 'could not be read (absent)' but will never come back; (b) a WIP '0 / 8 in flight vs the declared ceiling' from the retired operating model; (c) THE WORK-STORE PANEL, which is the bad one -- src/web/api/routers/work.py:482-488 prints 'A bug to fix still goes to the review backlogs', instructing every reader to file into registers that are archived and unread. [!] THAT PANEL IS ACTIVE MISINFORMATION ON THE ONE PAGE BUILT TO PREVENT DROPPED WORK, so it outranks the rest of this row. It is a read path (Tier 1 per the tier table) but it is src/ and the route's tier must be checked against docs/api-tier-policy.md before editing. [!] THE LESSON FOR THE SWEEP ITSELF: 'grep the archived filenames' is the right probe but I ran it over the wrong POPULATION. The population is every consumer of an archived path ANYWHERE -- .github/, scripts/, src/, and the dashboard repo -- not the two directories I happened to be working in. [!] DISPATCHED 2026-09-21. MODEL UPGRADED haiku-4.5 -> sonnet-5, deliberately and against this row's own earlier value: this row's note records that the previous sweep ran over the WRONG POPULATION and that three of four orphan classes were found by something failing loudly or the operator looking at the page, not by the sweep. That is a judgement failure, not a throughput one, and haiku is the wrong instrument for it. The cheap-extraction half is instead being run SEPARATELY on the Fable pool as an independent cross-check (see E11) -- which gets the cheap model onto the cheap half without betting the sweep on it. [!] LANE TOLD the src/web/api/routers/work.py:482-488 panel OUTRANKS the 67 guard scripts, and that if budget runs short an honestly-bounded sweep REPORT beats a half-finished deletion pass. [!] THREE MORE INSTANCES FOUND ON 2026-09-21 WHILE THIS LANE WAS ALREADY RUNNING, all by running something rather than by a sweep, and they are FILED IN THE PIPELINE rather than added to this note so they cannot be lost if this lane lands without them: PI-20260921-0001 (trainer-VM serialization FIFO promised by two workflow comments, board archived -- routed to its own lane, session_01W7iGwkrozCQ8LYRSM8WgGE), PI-20260921-0002 (pr-landing-guard R13's first remedy message names the archived session-board.json, so every future Tier-1 self-landing PR is sent to a dead end before finding the working per-branch route), and PI-20260921-0003 (check_manager_scope.py derives WHO THE MANAGER IS from the archived MANAGER-LEASE.json, reports `no_manager_commits` on a branch with four manager commits, and EXITS 0 -- so the guard that enforces rule 1 of the manager contract fails OPEN while both CLAUDE.md and the manager SKILL still claim it is CI-enforced). [!] THE RUNNING TALLY IS NOW FIVE ORPHAN CLASSES AND FIVE FOUND THE HARD WAY. That is no longer an anecdote about one missed directory; it is evidence that a filename grep is the wrong PRIMARY probe. A guard or workflow that READS an archived register frequently does not name it in a greppable string at all -- it derives a path, or names it only in prose while the code reads a directory. The probe that actually caught 0002 and 0003 was RUNNING THE THING AND READING WHAT IT SAID. Consider adding that to this row's method: execute every guard in run_guards.py and every self-test, and treat `could not check`, `does not exist` and a green-on-nothing as findings. [!] CEILING BREACHED 2026-09-21: $22.73 against $20. Not killed -- the contract says read what the lane produced first, and the work is delivered in PR #12680. [!] BUT THE SWEEP IS INCOMPLETE and the Fable cross-check is how we know, which is exactly why E11 ran in parallel. E9 fixed the three Workflow-page panels (the operator-facing misinformation, which was the highest-value half and is done) and filed four pipeline rows, but did not reach the session-start hooks, CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL, the live-money runtime ping, or the five guards-reporting-clean-over-nothing. That is simply wrong -- `landed_unproven` means MERGED with the effect not yet observed, and nothing here is merged. Set back to `in_flight`. Caught by close-out check 3, which is the check that exists for exactly this, and worth recording because the error runs in the DANGEROUS direction: a row reading `landed_unproven` tells the next session the code is on main and only the observation is outstanding, so it would not have looked for an unmerged PR. [!] STATE CORRECTED AT CLOSE-OUT: the row read `in_flight` against an archived lane. Its PR (#12680) is MERGED, but the row was always going to outlive it -- E11's independent Fable probe reached four live reader surfaces this sweep did not, and PI-20260921-0001's lane flagged ~20+ non-archived files still live-reading board-pointer.json / session-board.json. items.title: armed-branch-push-watch races PR creation — every post-merge follow-up trips it
items.note: MEASURED 2026-09-21 on PR #12673, which is the follow-up to the reset's own merge. scripts/ci/check_armed_branch_push.py reported `dropped` (error, exit 1) on a HEALTHY push. Timing is the whole bug: #12668 squash-merged as 3ea2777 at 12:18 and GitHub deleted the branch; the branch was reset from the new main and A6 pushed at 12:25:43; #12673 was opened at 12:26:10. The watcher ran in that 27-second gap, when the branch's ONLY associated PR was the merged #12668 whose head.sha (1d596e2) is not the pushed sha (f3301d0). [!] THIS IS NOT A ONE-OFF. A PR cannot be opened for a branch that has not been pushed, so EVERY follow-up PR made the sanctioned way (git fetch origin main && git checkout -B <branch> origin/main) trips this between push and PR creation. The guard's premise -- that the PR it finds is the PR for this push -- is false during a branch reset. [!] DO NOT 'FIX' IT BY DOWNGRADING THE SEVERITY. The loss it exists for (#11846) is real, and a guard that cries wolf on the healthy path is how a guard gets ignored -- the desensitisation this repo already measured at 202 of 376 CRITICALs being one un-latched condition. Sharpen the condition. [!] THE DISCRIMINATOR, and it does NOT fall into the ancestry trap the script's own docstring warns about. That trap is asking whether a BRANCH commit reached main -- which a squash merge always answers no to. Ask the OPPOSITE: is the old PR's MERGE COMMIT an ancestor of the PUSHED commit? Branch correctly reset -> yes (3ea2777 is an ancestor of f3301d0), nothing lost, a new PR is coming. Genuine drop, i.e. more commits pushed onto the merged branch's old history -> no; the pre-merge head is the ancestor instead. A squash does not defeat that direction. [!] The script has an elaborate --self-test with a mutation-tested exact-sha comparison; extend it rather than loosening it, and add the branch-reset case as a NAMED fixture so the next person cannot re-introduce this by tightening something else. [!] DISPATCHED 2026-09-21, sonnet-5, fresh, ceiling $12 (this row carried no ceiling; one is set now). It earns its slot today because the manager's own pushes are the population it mis-grades: every follow-up PR made the sanctioned way trips it in the gap between push and PR creation. Lane told in terms to SHARPEN the condition and NOT downgrade the severity, and to CONSTRUCT both cases rather than implement the proposed discriminator on trust -- a reported hole beats a confident fix. [!] CLOSED 2026-09-21 AS ALREADY FIXED, AND THE LANE THAT ESTABLISHED IT WAS DISPATCHED IN ERROR BY THIS MANAGER. The fix landed in #12676 -- the SAME PR the handoff named as 'A7's pipeline + close-out contract + E10' -- and this row was never moved off `queued`. VERIFIED on main, not taken from the lane: scripts/ci/check_armed_branch_push.py defines RESET_FROM_MERGE, carries the merge-commit-ancestry discriminator, and has the branch-reset case as a named self-test fixture. Cost of the error: $0.93. [!] THE LESSON IS NOT 'READ MORE CAREFULLY', it is that a row's `state` was not moved by the PR that resolved it, so the register lied to the next reader in the direction of MORE work rather than less. Filed as PI-20260921-M06.

items.title: Employ the Fable weekly allowance — decide WHICH task classes, by measurement
items.note: [2026-10-01T16:45Z manager session_01MM8o5js6TcDFeNAPBY4Ntv] Operator-directed manager handoff (docs/claude/work/MANAGER-HANDOFF-2026-10-01.md, PR #15219): the owning manager is now session_01MM8o5js6TcDFeNAPBY4Ntv, replacing session_01HYq6XtfesZ57VyaQrK6CL1. || OPERATOR DIRECTIVE 2026-09-21, verbatim: 'it should definitely be used when appropriate -- we want to employ that budget as well, we just want to make sure it is getting the tasks that are the best use of that resource.' So this row is NOT 'should we use it'. It is 'what goes there', and the answer must be measured rather than assumed. [!] WHY IT IS FREE CAPACITY: Settings > Usage shows Fable on a SEPARATE weekly limit from the main pool, measured 2026-09-21 at 0% used against a main pool at 68%. Work routed to Fable does not draw down the allowance the other lanes pace against, so this is additive headroom, not a trade-off between lanes. [!] THE SELECTION METHOD, because 'seems like a good fit' is how the wrong work lands on the wrong model. Pick the first class by ONE property: its output must be CHEAPLY VERIFIABLE against ground truth that already exists, so a bad fit is caught on the first run instead of propagating into a register. Run it on inputs a current-model lane has ALREADY done, diff the outputs, and widen only on that evidence. State the population of any quality claim, per RULE ONE. [!] WHAT THIS ROW MAY NOT DO, and it is the one hard edge: budget headroom is NEVER a reason to move work off the model its risk demands. .claude/skills/manager/SKILL.md already binds 'anything on a real-money order path' to opus. A cheaper pool does not relax that, and 'we had Fable budget spare' is not an argument that may ever appear next to an order-path change. [!] NOTHING IS MEASURED YET. No claim about Fable's fit for any lane in this repo has been made or tested as of 2026-09-21 -- the only established facts are that the pool exists, is separate, and is unused. Do not read a task list into this row that is not here. [!] FIRST FABLE ROUTING DECIDED AND DISPATCHED 2026-09-21, and the class chosen is GREP-AND-CLASSIFY SWEEP OVER A REPOSITORY. Chosen by this row's own stated method -- 'start with a class whose output is cheaply verifiable against work a current-model lane has already done, diff the two, and widen only on that evidence' -- so the probe runs IN PARALLEL with E9's sonnet sweep over the same needle set, and the diff is the measurement. [!] THE DUPLICATION IS THE DESIGN, not waste: Fable is a SEPARATE weekly allowance measured at 0% used, so this lane costs the main pool nothing and is additive capacity. [!] IT IS ALSO A REAL CROSS-CHECK regardless of what the diff shows, because this exact sweep has already been run once over the wrong population and missed src/web/api/ entirely. [!] SCOPED REPORT-ONLY -- one markdown file, no code changes, no fixes -- so a weak result costs a file nobody merges rather than a bad edit in src/. Given the three known positives as a mandatory probe control. [!] DO NOT read a good result here as authorising Fable on an order path: spare budget never moves work off the model its risk demands. [!] EARLY READ 2026-09-21, reported as an in-flight observation and NOT as the measurement: the Fable lane found all three mandated positive controls and was analysing a 2,090-line grep result while two of the five main-pool lanes were still stalled at zero work on an authenticity check. That is a signal about SPAWN HYGIENE (PI-20260921-0004), not about model quality, and must not be read as one -- the lanes that stalled had not started, so there is nothing to compare yet. The measurement is the DIFF against E9's sweep and it is not available until both land. [!] MEASURED AND DECIDED 2026-09-21. THE FABLE ROUTING IS VALIDATED FOR THIS CLASS and the evidence is not a vibe: the probe stated its population (282 archived basenames + 10 retired skill names + 6 work-store subdirs, over 8,540 tracked files, 2,931 hit lines in 1,197 files), found ALL THREE mandated positive controls including the one the previous sweep missed, gave its own methodology an honest caveat unprompted (`duty` is an English word, so set B was searched only in skill-reference shapes and a plain-prose mention is NOT in the report), and carried a 'what I could not determine' section. [!] IT ALSO OUT-FOUND THE SONNET LANE IT WAS RUN AGAINST, which is the diff E11 existed to produce: four live READER surfaces E9 did not reach, three of them user-facing -- the session-start hooks (PI-20260921-M05), docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md contradicting CLAUDE.md, the live-money runtime telling the operator to run an archived skill, and five CI guards reporting `clean` over an empty population. [!] CEILING BREACHED: $14.95 against $10. Read before judged, per the contract -- the overrun bought the population count and the classifier, which are the parts that make it checkable, so this is a ceiling set too low for the task rather than a lane that sprawled. Next sweep of this class gets $20. [!] WHAT THIS DOES NOT LICENSE: a good result on a bounded read-only sweep says nothing about an order path, and spare budget never moves work off the model its risk demands. || 2026-10-01 ~11:25Z (manager session_01HYq6XtfesZ57VyaQrK6CL1): WIDENED BY MEASUREMENT: pre-merge independent PR reviews now run on Fable. Evidence (population: 2 replay reviews on historical heads whose blockers a main-model review had already found, plus 3 live reviews): replay of #15070@afe7364 found the known Positions/Orders-row click AND a new circular-verification bug; replay of #15075@6c9ec8a found the known Positions-table blocker by a different mechanism AND a residual on main (variant b), reproduced in Chromium. items.title: Prop: no fill since 2026-08-30, and the status ask fires on the wrong trigger
items.note: OPERATOR-RAISED 2026-09-21, unprompted, in their own words: 'I haven't gotten any trade notifications there in a suspiciously long time, and I keep getting the prop status request notifications even though we said we don't need that anymore -- I give the snapshot when a trade closes and the account doesn't need to be tracked actively when there's no activity.' [!] MEASURED off the live host the same hour (direct over ict-bot.duckdns.org, not from a doc): newest account_status is id 19 at 2026-08-30T19:33:29Z -- status_age_hours 528.4 against a 24h threshold, freshness `stale`. distance_to_dd_floor_usd reads $87.34 against the $4,700 static floor, computed off that 22-day-old snapshot; distance_to_daily_loss_usd is null (day_pnl_state `realized_unreported`), so the daily-loss half of the account-killer guard is NOT COMPUTED AT ALL. Newest ticket 2026-09-13 `expired`; everything back to 2026-08-30 `suppressed`/`skipped`. reconcile: 92 tickets, 43 fills, 0 unacted. [!] SO THE STRATEGY SIDE IS ALIVE AND NOTHING REACHES A FILL -- that is the shape of the question, and the lane's first job is to say WHICH of four candidates is true with a stated population, not to adopt the tidy one. The manager's leading hypothesis (sizing refusing on the stale balance) is EXPLICITLY CHALLENGED on the row: a ticket was emitted 2026-09-13, fourteen days past the snapshot, so sizing did not refuse on that tick. [!] OPERATOR DECISION 2026-09-21 (popup, direct): the status ask fires ONLY ON NEW EXPOSURE -- at the moment a real, non-suppressed ticket is about to take exposure. The flat-book cadence goes. They were shown the $87.34-on-a-22-day-old-number cushion and the cost of going quiet while flat, and chose this. prop_status_request.py's docstring argues WELL against it (the static-DD floor binds while flat); that argument is to be KEPT and the decision recorded beside it, dated and attributed -- not deleted. [!] OPERATOR CONFIRMED, asked directly: breakout_1 is funded, live, and SHOULD be trading. So the silence is a defect, not the expected state. [!] THE PIPELINE PREDICTED THIS EXACT DAY. BL-20260909-PROP-SIZING-REFUSAL-ON-A-STALE-BALANCE-IS-JOURNALED-BUT-NEVER-PINGED has been open since 2026-09-09 and its clears_when says in terms: 'breakout_1 can stop trading indefinitely with the only evidence being a journalctl line.' The operator found it from the outside, by noticing an absence of notifications -- the worst available discovery method, and the second time today that the operator's own eyes beat a sweep. [!] SO SILENCING THE ASK DOES NOT SHIP ALONE: the periodic ask was the only thing that happened to be noisy in the stalled state, so removing it makes the silent stall strictly worse. The refusal path gets an operator-facing signal in the same landing. [!] LANE FENCED OUT of changing sizing logic, breakout_executor's suppression rule, and anything on the order path -- a diagnosis pointing there comes BACK as a proposal. PROP IS REAL MONEY: routed to opus for that reason, against the model table's order-path line. [!] MERGED 2026-09-21 as 635600c, Tier-2, OPERATOR APPROVED after being shown what it does. [!] THE ROOT CAUSE IS FOUND AND IS NOT WHAT ANYONE GUESSED -- and the manager's leading hypothesis (sizing refusing on the stale balance) was REFUTED twice, independently. TWO INDIVIDUALLY-CORRECT TIER-3 CHANGES COMPOSED INTO A SILENT OUTAGE: 2026-08-23 removed the base twins from breakout_1's roster (approved de-dup), and 2026-08-31 rewrote _election_sort_key so the base twin now wins a tie against its _prop sibling. The twins carry IDENTICAL entry parameters, so both fire on every breakout bar, one global winner is elected per symbol, and since 2026-08-31 the winner is always the base twin -- which is not on breakout_1. MEASURED 21 of 21 contested packages to the base twin; breakout_1 received none. No ticket, no suppressed row, no rejection, no log line naming the account. [!] THE ASK WAS A LATCH, established before anything was changed: a 2026-09-13 ticket with a 1h TTL expired unanswered, `expired` was not in NON_EXPOSING_TICKET_STATUSES, and the arm compared against a snapshot only an OPERATOR REPORT can move -- so it asked every 12h forever for the report it was asking for. Fixed as a class (`ticket_can_take_exposure`), not as an instance. [!] landed_unproven, NOT done: BL-20260909 is MOVED not closed (its clears_when needs the refusal observed reaching a channel on the live host after deploy), and the OUTAGE ITSELF IS UNFIXED -- that is E17. [!] CLOSING THIS ROW MEANS TWO OBSERVATIONS, AND THEY ARE SEPARATE. (a) The status ask: a 12-hourly prop status-request ping does NOT arrive while the book is flat and no ticket can take exposure -- the operator noticing its ABSENCE over a few days, since the fix is the removal of a signal and there is nothing positive to see. (b) The sizing-refusal page: a `prop_sizing_refusal` observed reaching an operator-facing channel on the live host after deploy, which is BL-20260909's own clears_when and currently unmakeable while the diag relay is down (E19). ⚠️ NEITHER closes the OUTAGE -- breakout_1 receiving a ticket again is E17. [2026-09-25 sweep] (a) Live state (diag log_file prop_status_request) shows the last ask fired on last_verdict=position_open, matching the new trigger, not cadence -- but breakout_1 hasn't been flat long enough since the fix to observe an absence; recheck once it goes flat for >=48h. (b) operator_alerts.jsonl (2026-09-18 to 09-25, direct diag read, 301 entries) has zero prop_sizing_refusal or any prop-kind entries -- no refusal event has occurred to test the channel. Note: E19 is actually done and the diag relay is directly reachable (verified this session) -- (b)'s blocker is that the triggering event hasn't happened, not the relay.

[!] THIS ROW DOES NOT REACH `done` ON THE WRITE. get-env reports `pending_restart` when the .env was edited and the service never re-read it, so the write alone proves nothing. Closing it needs an arbitration round ACTUALLY APPLYING for breakout_1 -- rounds_applied carrying its leg, not just rounds_planned.

[!!] DIAGNOSIS FALSIFIED 2026-09-24T09:55Z, BEFORE ANY CHANGE WAS MADE. The fix this row specifies -- 'add breakout_1 to ARBITRATION_FANOUT_ACCOUNTS via set-env' -- WOULD HAVE BEEN A NO-OP, and the manager was one dispatch away from making it and reporting E17 fixed. The read-before-write the row itself demanded is the only reason it did not happen.
MEASURED, three reads, each naming its source:
  (1) get-env ARBITRATION_FANOUT_ACCOUNTS (issue #12804) -- breakout_1 IS ALREADY PRESENT, on BOTH the running process and the declared env file, alongside all 10 other accounts. allowlisted_accounts() reads exactly that variable and splits on commas, so apply_scope_for('breakout_1','apply') must return `allowlisted` today.
  (2) get-env ARBITRATION_FANOUT_MODE (issue #12822) -- process 'apply', declared 'apply'. The mode is ARMED, so the soak is not silent because it was switched off.
  (3) diag log_file arbitration_fanout_soak (issue #12820) -- THE NEWEST ROW IS 2026-09-23T01:52:51Z, about 32 hours stale. The last 35 rows span 2026-09-22T16:51 to 2026-09-23T01:52 and contain ZERO breakout_1, ZERO not_allowlisted, ZERO non-zero starved_count.
[!] SO THE ROW'S EVIDENCE IS UNVERIFIABLE, NOT DISPROVEN, and the distinction is the point. apply_scope {breakout_1: 'not_allowlisted'} with starved_count 1 may well have been true when the lane read it; what is established now is that it CANNOT BE REPRODUCED, because the log that produced it stopped. Do not rewrite the history as 'the lane was wrong' -- it read something this session cannot re-read.
[!] WHY THE SILENCE IS ANOMALOUS RATHER THAN QUIET, read from code: intent_multiplexer.py calls arbitration_fanout_soak.record() on EVERY arbitration where a winning intent is decided, and record() returns early only on mode == 'off'. It is NOT gated on having multiple candidates the way allocator_soak is. And its call site swallows exceptions by design so an observe-only soak can never break a tick -- which also means a BROKEN soak is invisible. 32 hours of nothing, with mode=apply, is a defect and not an absence of contested elections.
[!] STATE IS `blocked`, NOT `in_flight`, and the edge is the soak. The manager set this row in_flight earlier today on the strength of a diagnosis that these three reads have since overtaken; leaving it in_flight would hand the next session a live lane pointed at a no-op. NOTHING WAS DISPATCHED: no set-env was run.
[!] WHAT THE NEXT SESSION SHOULD DO, in order: fix or explain the soak (PI-20260924-JN54P2HH-0004) so the mechanism is observable again; THEN re-read apply_scope for breakout_1; THEN decide. The original question -- why breakout_1 receives nothing -- IS STILL OPEN and is no longer answered by the allowlist.

items.title: The manager-scope guard's identity source was archived, so it reported PASS on a manager doing items — plus three cost leaks
items.note:
[!] THE E20 LANE HAS STOPPED — NOBODY IS WORKING THIS ROW. Work complete in two PRs, BOTH MERGE-PENDING with auto-merge armed: #12740 (the guard's identity + fail-closed + the planted 2026-09-21 regression) and #12742 (the three cost causes, the reconciler, the manager SKILL.md controls). `lane` is deliberately null rather than still naming the session: lane_reconcile.py's own `in_flight with NO lane` check now fires on this row, which is the correct alarm. MOVE THIS TO `landed_unproven` WHEN BOTH MERGE, and to `done` on the observation named at the end of this note. === WHAT WAS DELIVERED. (A) THE ROOT CAUSE, WHICH IS BIGGER THAN THE THREE COST LEAKS: scripts/ci/check_manager_scope.py derived manager identity only from MANAGER-LEASE.json, which the 2026-09-21 reset ARCHIVED, so the roster froze at 7 sessions (last run ending 2026-09-19T10:42:44Z) and could never grow. RE-VERIFIED every line rather than trusting the dispatch. MEASURED FURTHER: that day's manager has 38 commits, 31 off MANAGER_SURFACE (config/accounts.yaml x6, tests x5, scripts/ops x4, src/web/api/routers/work.py x2, scripts/ci x1), every one graded `not_manager` and skipped. FIXED: identity is now the UNION of derived sources; new `dispatch` source = a commit newly setting a row's `lane` to a session OTHER than its own. MEASURED over 635 commits: 12 dispatch acts, 1 session named, FALSE POSITIVES 0 of 1, the 6 self-lane-only sessions NOT admitted, FALSE NEGATIVES 7 of 7 vs the lease and STRUCTURAL (pre-reset `lane` held a team name: engineering 30, ops 29, research 18, zero session ids) which is why both sources stay. INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED by a surface I did not use: list_sessions' own `parent_session_id` names exactly 2 managers across 58 lanes — that day's (found by dispatch) and session_01GHpyXT2qssLJsrvXBQRkQF (found by the lease). The union covers both. (B) IT FAILS CLOSED, which matters more: no live identity source -> `no_identity_source`, live source with an empty roster -> `identity_unresolved`, BOTH FAIL at EXIT 2 (distinct from 1 for a real finding). It previously returned 7 stale ids and carried on. (C) THE REGRESSION IS PLANTED: --self-test 33 -> 40 cases. (D) THE TRAP WAS NOT WALKED INTO: 18 of the 38 still FAIL R2 after the change. Two paths were admitted, each the moved subject of an already-argued rule: .github/merge-slots/** graded PER COMMIT (own branch only), and research/queue/** as the surviving half of the 2026-09-03 operator ruling that filing is management. (E) THE THREE COST CAUSES, MEASURED LIVE 2026-09-22T13:02Z over the 60 most recent sessions, $5,892.69 readable of 51 of 60: 14 lanes over ceiling (B1 12.4x, not the six this row said — the row read running totals, its own cause 1); 22 finished-but-unarchived sessions holding $2,088.73; 4 BLOCKED lanes holding $1,347.60. [!] THE HEADLINE AND IT IS 30x THIS ROW'S ESTIMATE: session_01XYu2vvg9Qgxoqf4jJQyd8i (ENGINEERING LANE MI-305, spawned by the PREVIOUS manager 2026-09-18) has sat BLOCKED and IDLE 72.8 hours holding $1,343.06 and has NEVER COMMITTED A LINE — more than this row's entire 13-lane day in one session that produced nothing. Filed as PI-20260922-ONE-BLOCKED-LANE-HAS-HELD-1343-USD-FOR-72-HOURS-HAVING-NEVER-COMMITTED-A-LINE-AND-22-FINISHED-LANES-SIT-UNARCHIVED. A walled lane needs a HUMAN to clear its prompt and archiving another manager's lanes is the MANAGER's call, so it is surfaced, not cleared. (F) THE INVOLUNTARY MECHANISM IS BUILT, TRIED AND HONESTLY NOT WORKING. Two cheaper designs were KILLED ON MEASUREMENT first: a CI guard on git commit recency (5 of 7 WORKING lanes had NEVER committed, so it would have redded five healthy lanes) and a CI guard on the offline half (it would fail contributors for the manager's behaviour). The chosen design — a Routine firing a FRESH session, so the manager is not in the path — was created, FIRED ONCE, and DISABLED the same minute: the fired session has no repo checkout and no MCP connectors, so it can neither run the script nor call list_sessions. THE INVARIANT IS THEREFORE STILL VOLUNTARY and says so; what stands is a DISCIPLINE in SKILL.md, labelled as one. Filed as PI-20260922-THE-LANE-WATCHDOG-ROUTINE-FIRES-SESSIONS-WITH-NO-REPO-AND-NO-MCP-SO-IT-IS-DISABLED-AND-THE-INVARIANT-IS-STILL-VOLUNTARY — the operator must attach the connector + source in the Routines UI, which a session cannot do. (G) ALSO FILED, found while fixing R2 and not walked past: R6/R7/R8's subjects are ALL absent on main too, so three of four rules grade nothing and two did it silently — PI-20260922-MANAGER-SCOPE-R6-R7-R8-HAVE-NO-SUBJECT-AFTER-THE-RESET-SO-THREE-OF-FOUR-RULES-GRADE-NOTHING. === REACHED: MERGED is not yet true (both PRs armed, not merged). DEPLOYED and OBSERVED are not claimed for anything in this row. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: check_manager_scope.py printing `identity source `dispatch`: live` with the current manager on the roster, AND a `violation` on a real PR graded from main rather than from a branch. === WHAT THIS ROW'S ORIGINAL TEXT GOT WRONG, kept so it is not re-quoted: 'six lanes exceeded theirs' is 14 when measured after archiving, and 'final spends read off get_session' is only true via external_metadata.usage.cost_usd, which is ABSENT on 9 of 60 sessions — 6 of them WORKING — so an unreadable cost must render as could-not-look, never $0. === ORIGINAL ROW TEXT FOLLOWS === MEASURED 2026-09-21 across 12 dispatched lanes, final spends read off get_session: roughly $860 against ceilings totalling ~$250. Six lanes exceeded theirs; two exceeded by more than 6x (B1 $270.39/$35, B2 $229.13/$30). [!] THREE DISTINCT CAUSES, and they need different fixes -- lumping them as 'lanes are expensive' would fix none. (1) A CEILING NOBODY CHECKS MID-FLIGHT IS NOT A CEILING. Nothing reads spend during a run; the manager set ceilings and looked once, at the end. A1's meter now exists and this is its first real consumer. (2) FINISHED LANES KEEP SPENDING. A9 went $37.13 -> $50.78 AFTER its work merged, sitting subscribed to its own PR; E16 went $25.38 -> $56.14 the same way. Watching a PR is not free and the lane has nothing left to contribute to it. Archive on merge, or do not subscribe a lane to the PR the manager is going to merge anyway. (3) AN UNATTENDED LANE CAN HIT AN INTERACTIVE PERMISSION PROMPT AND SPEND ITS WHOLE BUDGET THERE. B2 did, twice. The second attempt's pending action was readable and specific: a COMPOUND, PIPED git command (`git fetch ... 2>&1 | tail -5 && git merge ... 2>&1 | tail -60`) awaiting a Bash approval nobody was present to give. ⚠️ THAT COMMAND SHAPE IS A HYPOTHESIS, NOT ESTABLISHED -- other lanes committed and pushed all day, so it is not universal. Establish WHICH shapes are refused before writing a rule about it; a dispatch instruction based on a guess would be the same category of error this repo keeps paying for. [!] THE CHEAPEST FIX IS PROBABLY (2) AND IT IS FREE: stop subscribing lanes to PRs the manager merges. [!] ⚠️ THE TOTAL ON THIS ROW WAS WRONG WHEN IT WAS WRITTEN, AND THE ERROR WAS THIS ROW'S OWN CAUSE (1). It said ~$860. Read again after every lane was ARCHIVED, the total is ~$1,142 across 13 lanes. B1 alone is $435.05, not the $270.39 committed a few hours earlier -- it accrued $165 MORE while IDLE, watching the PR the manager was about to merge anyway. A1 is $59.17, not $28.03. [!] SO THE MANAGER MADE THE SAME MISTAKE TWICE IN ONE DAY, the second time inside the commit describing the mistake. The mechanism is exact and unglamorous: get_session on a LIVE lane returns a RUNNING total, and a running total written onto a row reads like a final one. [!] THE RULE IS MECHANICAL, NOT 'be more careful': A LANE'S SPEND IS FINAL ONLY ONCE THE LANE IS ARCHIVED. Read it there, or record it with the read-time and the word `running` beside it. A number with no read-time is the same defect as a count that cannot say whether anyone looked. [!] AND IT SHARPENS CAUSE (2) from 'lanes keep spending' into a SIZE: the idle-watching tail is the single largest line in the day's spend, larger than any lane's actual work. [!] AND ONE MORE INSTANCE, CAUGHT IN THE ACT WHILE WRITING THIS ROW: resolving the checklist conflict with a 'longest note wins' heuristic silently reverted B1's state from `done` to `in_flight`. A heuristic that cannot say WHY it chose a side is the same defect as a count that cannot say whether anyone looked. States are now set explicitly from the merges performed, and the heuristic is not reused.  === E20 LANE UPDATE 2026-09-22 (session_011xpvJ2MQgd4jmKkdfg6gzV, branch claude/e20-manager-identity-fail-closed). THE ROOT CAUSE IS BIGGER THAN THE THREE COST LEAKS AND IS FIXED FIRST. RE-VERIFIED EVERY LINE rather than taken from the dispatch: lease_holders() -> 7 sessions across 478 revisions of MANAGER-LEASE.json, every lease-holding run ending 2026-09-19T10:42:44Z; MANAGER-LEASE.json ABSENT on origin/main (archived by the reset); session_01XQhayAHWdrSYv8jN54P2HH NOT on the roster. MEASURED FURTHER, which the dispatch did not state: that session has 38 commits and 31 touch a path off MANAGER_SURFACE -- config/accounts.yaml x6, tests/** x5, scripts/ops/** x4, src/web/api/routers/work.py x2, scripts/ci/** x1 -- and every one graded `not_manager` and was skipped. [!] IDENTITY IS NOW A UNION OF DERIVED SOURCES. New source `dispatch`: a commit that newly sets a row's `lane` to a session OTHER than its own trailer's. MEASURED over 635 commits touching this file: 12 dispatch acts naming 1 session -- that day's manager. FALSE POSITIVES 0 of 1. The 6 sessions that set a lane only to THEMSELVES are NOT admitted, which is the over-capture `updated_by` would have produced. FALSE NEGATIVES 7 of 7 against the lease roster, and STRUCTURAL not a flaw: pre-reset `lane` held a TEAM NAME (engineering 30, ops 29, research 18, zero session ids), so the signal did not exist before 2026-09-21 -- hence the union, in which a retired source keeps contributing history and simply cannot grow. [!] AND THE HALF THAT MATTERS MORE: IT FAILS CLOSED. Each source declares the path whose presence at HEAD decides whether it can grow (live/retired/unreadable, never collapsed). No live source -> `no_identity_source`; live source with an empty roster -> `identity_unresolved`. BOTH FAIL AT EXIT 2, distinct from exit 1 for a real finding, per the canonical doc's `could not measure is its own outcome`. Previously an empty roster returned 7 stale ids and carried on, or state `unattributed` and exit 0. [!] THE 2026-09-21 REGRESSION IS PLANTED: --self-test goes 33 -> 40 cases, including `lease archived + manager identified only by dispatch -> violation` (without the second source it is `no_manager_commits`, a pass) and `every subject removed -> exit 2`. `exit_code` is a function so the test asserts the exit code instead of the docstring claiming it. [!] REPORTED, NOT WALKED PAST: R6/R7/R8 have no subject either -- SESSIONS.json, MERGE-QUEUE.json and the lease are all absent on main, so three of four rules grade NOTHING and two did it silently. Every run now prints a RULE LIVENESS block. Filed as PI-20260922-MANAGER-SCOPE-R6-R7-R8-HAVE-NO-SUBJECT-AFTER-THE-RESET-SO-THREE-OF-FOUR-RULES-GRADE-NOTHING with a rerun; retiring vs re-pointing them is an operator decision, not this lane's. [!] THE TRAP WAS NOT WALKED INTO: MANAGER_SURFACE is not widened until the manager's commits pass. AFTER this change 18 of the 38 still FAIL R2 (4 more are under active dated exceptions, 7 are per-branch merge-slot claims, 7 were already on the surface). Two paths were admitted, each as the moved subject of an already-argued rule and neither wholesale: .github/merge-slots/** graded PER COMMIT by branch_slot_claim_only (own branch only), the successor of the session-board merge_slot carve-out the same reset archived; and research/queue/** as the surviving half of the 2026-09-03 OPERATOR RULING that filing is management, whose named file (health-review-backlog.json) the reset also archived. [!] (4) AND (5) ARE DELIVERED in #12742, not outstanding: the three cost causes measured live, the reconciler extended with fmt_cost refusing a bare spend figure, and the manager SKILL.md controls. [!] PLUS A FOURTH THING THE MANAGER HANDED THIS LANE MID-SESSION, because it is the same defect class: check_manager_queue_watch reporting NEVER_RAN_OVERDUE after 479 hours and zero receipts. ROOT-CAUSED AT THE PRIMARY SOURCE and it is the SAME cause as this lane's own failed watchdog — a Routine-fired session gets NO repo checkout and NO mcp__ connectors, so that Routine could never perform either half of its own prompt, while firing hourly and reporting SUCCEEDED (~479 firings, roughly $90). Two independent Routines, same two absences, with the negative control run (an ordinary lane DOES return session_context.sources). DISPOSITION: do NOT retire the guard — it is the only thing that noticed; the decision is about the ROUTINES and only the operator can grant what they need. [!] AND THE SWEEP THE MANAGER ASKED FOR, with its population: 95 guard scripts, every module-level repo-path constant tested against HEAD. FOUR STATES: 46 no_declared_subject (the instrument cannot speak to them, counted separately and never folded into live), 30 live, 11 DEGRADED, 8 DEAD — grading nothing. All 19 are the 2026-09-21 reset's blast radius, and THREE OF THE DEAD (check_claim_basis, check_soak_registered, check_operator_owed) are named in docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md as LIVE MECHANISMS. Mechanism: scripts/ci/check_guard_liveness.py, WIRED into run_guards.py, report-first with a shrink-only baseline so it does not red-wall the repo on day one. [!] AND THE STRUCTURAL HALF, built after the manager supplied the design constraint that FRESHNESS BELONGS IN CI RATHER THAN ON A TIMER — because the obvious fix (emit receipts, grade their freshness) IS check_manager_queue_watch, i.e. instance #3, so a scheduled grader can always be the thing that did not fire while CI's own liveness is proven by PRs merging at all. scripts/ci/check_cadence_liveness.py, WIRED as `cadence-liveness`, DERIVES its population from the tree (workflow `schedule:` crons + deploy/*.timer OnCalendar) and FAILS on anything derived-but-unregistered, so omission is detectable rather than a hand-maintained list. The 37 split into 8 that already commit back (one declared output path from gradeable, the cheap shrink) and 29 with no in-repo trace at all. [!] RESIDUAL NAMED IN A DISCLOSURE PRINTED ON EVERY RUN: a ROUTINE is not derivable from the repo, so a Routine's omission is NOT detected — and instance #3 was a Routine. Both halves of this class bottom out in the SAME operator action: attach the connector and a source to the Routines, or delete them.
