items.title: The partial ARBITRATION_FANOUT_ACCOUNTS allowlist SUBTRACTS bybit_2 and bybit_portfolio from rounds they had already won — armed for one account, the fan-out is narrower than unarmed
items.note: OPERATOR-RAISED 2026-09-22, from the numbers: '200 trades on paper and one on money for the same time frame seems out of whack... We need to verify that and see why that is.' VERIFIED, THEY ARE RIGHT. [!] MEASURED BY THE MANAGER, population stated: the 200 most recent closed trades, closedAt 2026-09-13T20:55:29Z -> 2026-09-22T08:48:49Z (~9 days), restricted to the six legs bybit_2 was actually running (its pre-R2 roster), counted per account — bybit_1 12, bybit_2 1, bybit_portfolio 1. The MIRROR agreeing with bybit_2 rather than with bybit_1 is what ruled out a broker fault and pointed at routing. That is the 12/1/1 figure the lane's note below calls inherited: it is inherited from this measurement, not from prose. THE OPERATOR'S DIRECTIVE (2026-09-22) IS RECORDED IN THE MEMO VERBATIM AND NOTHING IN THE REPO STATED IT BEFORE: bybit_1 is the SOAK INSTRUMENT and must never constrain another account; bybit_2 (real money) and bybit_portfolio (its paper mirror) trade the same things; arbitration is per-ACCOUNT, scoped to the candidates THAT account is considering. [!] THE FINDING, AND IT IS NOT THE ONE THIS ROW WAS DISPATCHED ON. The starvation of bybit_2 is not only BL-20260827's global winner-per-symbol. It is a SECOND, NEWER mechanism: arming ARBITRATION_FANOUT_ACCOUNTS for bybit_1 ALONE made routing STRICTLY NARROWER THAN LEAVING IT UNARMED. pipeline.py:1087 dispatches the fan-out as `if _rounds: <per-round> else: <global>` -- it REPLACES the global dispatch -- and _attach_fanout_plan narrows every round through scope_round_to_accounts(r, allow), which INTERSECTS the round's accounts with the allowlist. So one surviving bybit_1 round suppresses the global dispatch for that tick and every non-allowlisted account in that round is DELETED from a dispatch the global path would have served. [!] MEASURED ON THE LIVE SOAK, locator: diag-request issue #12708, run 35695727461, read 2026-09-22T06:38:27Z, path log_file?name=arbitration_fanout_soak&lines=30. POPULATION, STATED: 11 complete rows + 1 truncated, 2026-09-21T14:52:12Z -> 21:17:33Z, ~6.4 HOURS -- NOT the ~9-day trade window the defect statement was measured over. The relay cut the container field at its 47739-byte budget. Positive control IS IN THE PULL: present true, size_bytes 1156308, rows parse, git_sha f3746abd1 == on-disk, restart_pending false. Every row carries fanout_schema 3, global_mode apply, apply_state dispatchable and a NON-EMPTY rounds_applied -- so the fan-out is not merely planning, IT IS THE LIVE DISPATCHER, and MI-286's projection defect is fixed and deployed. [!] THE ROW THAT SETTLES IT, 2026-09-21T20:30:08.586710Z ETHUSDT: accounts_planned 3, accounts_elected 3, elected_by_account = {bybit_1, bybit_2, bybit_portfolio} all -> trend_donchian_eth_4h, rounds_planned[0].accounts = [bybit_1, bybit_2, bybit_portfolio], rounds_written[0].accounts = [bybit_1], rounds_applied[0].accounts = [bybit_1]. The per-account election DID elect for real money and its mirror; the allowlist discarded them. The only thing between those two fields is scope_round_to_accounts. [!] REPRODUCED AGAINST THE REAL SOURCE (not re-typed), both branches, pinned in tests/test_arbitration_fanout_allowlist_scope.py, 8 passing. BEFORE/AFTER: on a co-election tick, unarmed -> bybit_2 ROUTED, allow={bybit_1} -> bybit_2 DROPPED, allow=all -> ROUTED. On a divergent tick (bybit_1 has 26 legs to bybit_2's 3, so this is the common case) the whole bybit_2 round returns None and vanishes while bybit_1's round still suppresses the global path. THE LIVE CONFIG IS THE ONLY ONE OF THE THREE THAT IS WORSE THAN DOING NOTHING. [!] WHY IT CLOSES THE 12/1/1 GAP: read from config/accounts.yaml, bybit_2 and bybit_portfolio run 3 legs (xrp_pullback_2h, trend_donchian_eth_4h, trend_donchian_xrp_4h) and ALL THREE are also on bybit_1's 26. So on EVERY tick bybit_2 has a candidate, bybit_1 has one too and one of the two branches fires: there is no tick on either of bybit_2's symbols on which the live config can dispatch it. bybit_portfolio is identical by CI construction, which is why the mirror agrees with bybit_2 rather than bybit_1 and why that agreement rules out a broker fault. [!] WINDOW BOUNDED, NOT DATED. The regression starts when MI-286's projection fix deployed (before it, accepted_rounds returned [] every tick and the pipeline always took the global else:). Its landing declaration is on main at or before 2026-09-17 -- the shallow-clone boundary this session could reach. I did NOT pin the deploy commit and the regression probably does NOT cover the earlier part of 2026-09-13->09-22; that part is BL-20260827. [!] SECOND DEFECT, FOUND ON THE WAY, NOT FIXED: on that same row starved_accounts is [] and starved_count is 0 WHILE TWO ACCOUNTS WERE DROPPED. arbitration_fanout.assess grades `starved` against the GLOBAL election and knows nothing of the allowlist, so starvation CAUSED BY THE FAN-OUT is invisible to starved_count and therefore to src/runtime/starved_account_alert.py. The only field pair that makes it sayable is rounds_planned vs rounds_written, and no alert reads it. Same class as E22/E31. Filed PI-20260922-FANOUT-STARVATION-INVISIBLE-TO-ASSESS. [!] PROPOSED, NOT LANDED (Tier 3). (a) get-env ARBITRATION_FANOUT_ACCOUNTS FIRST -- it is a CSV and EMPTY MEANS NONE -- then set-env the UNION with bybit_1,bybit_2,bybit_portfolio,breakout_1, service ict-trader-live, env_file shared. From the soak alone the live allowlist is known only to satisfy allow INTERSECT {bybit_1,bybit_2,bybit_portfolio,breakout_1} = {bybit_1}; it may hold Alpaca accounts this session cannot see, which is exactly why the read is not optional. (b) fix the scope in aggregate_intents so the election is per (symbol, account) at source. MY READ: the directive calls for BOTH, (b) is what 'obviously an incorrect application' means structurally and (a) is what 'immediately' means -- and (a) is not merely the fast path, because the live state is worse than unarmed. [!] I DELIBERATELY DID NOT WRITE (b)'S DIFF. plan_per_account_election's own docstring warns that re-running the aggregator per account re-emits a regime_hard_gate row per account per tick, corrupting the signal that partitions 'would have gated' from 'did gate' -- that is a design question, and shipping a diff I had not reasoned it through would be the improvisation E17 was told not to do. [!] THIRD OPTION, CHEAPEST, AND THE OPERATOR SHOULD BE OFFERED IT EXPLICITLY: set-env ARBITRATION_FANOUT_MODE=annotate. One variable, no roster question, returns routing to the global path -- strictly better than today for bybit_2 and no worse for anyone. It does not fix BL-20260827; it removes the regression while (b) is designed. [!] WHAT I COULD NOT DO, PLAINLY: issue_write returns 403 Resource not accessible by integration while issue_read on the same objects succeeds -- the write-scope boundary, not the transient token drop. SO I COULD NOT OPEN A FRESH DIAG-REQUEST and could not re-request the soak path alone for the untruncated tail; the measurement rests on rows recovered from the EXISTING #12708 comment. No file-drop relay exists for the live VM's diag surface (only the trainer VM), and https://ict-bot.duckdns.org/api/diag/* returns 401 without DIAG_READ_TOKEN, which this session does not hold. I also did NOT independently verify the 12/1/1 closed-trade split -- that needs /api/diag/audit_query behind the same relay; it is consistent with everything measured here but it is INHERITED, NOT RE-TAKEN. A session with a working issue_write should re-take ONE read -- log_file?name=arbitration_fanout_soak&lines=200 AS THE ONLY PATH IN THE ISSUE -- and count, over a stated window, rows where rounds_planned accounts strictly contain rounds_written accounts, and rows where a planned round was dropped entirely. [!] RELATION TO E17 (lane/e17-arm-arbitration-fanout-breakout1, blocked on the same 403): SAME VARIABLE, THIS ROW SUPERSEDES ITS FRAMING. E17 does not contradict this -- breakout_1 belongs in the union and (a) includes it -- but breakout_1 ALONE would not have helped bybit_2 or bybit_portfolio and would have left this regression running against real money. E17's own row says 'if it turns out the fanout runs and the record is merely missing, COME BACK, do not improvise'; the 2026-09-22 read established that it RUNS AND DISPATCHES, so that instruction is live. Its branch carries a checklist-note commit only -- no set-env, no code -- so nothing conflicts. RECOMMENDED DISPOSITION: fold E17 into this row's (a) as ONE wider set-env rather than two, because two sequential partial widenings mean an intermediate state in which some other account is the one being subtracted. [!] APPLIED AND VERIFIED ON THE RUNNING PROCESS, 2026-09-22, operator-approved twice. Sequence, each step with what it established: (1) READ FIRST, run 35718127262 -- ARBITRATION_FANOUT_ACCOUNTS process 'bybit_1', declared 'bybit_1', agreeing, no pending_restart. That resolved the lane's open caveat that the live allowlist might contain Alpaca accounts it could not see: it did not. (2) CHECKED BEFORE WRITING, because the memo's phrasing ('suppressed for that tick') would have implied cross-account contamination: pipeline.py computes _rounds = _fanout_apply_rounds(signal) PER SIGNAL, not per tick, so the suppression is scoped to one symbol's decision and Alpaca signals were never exposed to a Bybit round. (3) WRITE, run 35718253767 -- union to bybit_1,bybit_2,bybit_portfolio,breakout_1; .env updated; ict-trader-live.service restarted; Post-restart state active. (4) READ BACK, run 35718365883 -- process holds it. (5) OPERATOR EXTENDED IT ('yes, we need to add it for alpaca too'), run 35718739585, and the MANAGER WIDENED IT FURTHER TO ALL 11 ACCOUNTS -- stated as a judgement call, reversible with one set-env -- because a PARTIAL allowlist IS the defect: alpaca_live (3 legs, real money) has the identical shape to bybit_2 against alpaca_paper's 19-leg soak book, and ib_live/oanda_practice carry 0 legs so including them removes a latent hazard rather than creating one. Verified on the process, run 35718808115, process == declared, all 11. [!] DEPLOYED, NOT OBSERVED, AND THE DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THIS ROW. CLOSING IT MEANS, IN ORDER: a soak row on an ETHUSDT/XRPUSDT tick where rounds_written[].accounts == rounds_planned[].accounts, AND THEN a JOURNAL ROW FOR bybit_2 -- per the soak's own docstring, 'a soak row alone proves the decision, never the order'. [!] AND THIS IS A MITIGATION, NOT THE FIX: it removes the SUBTRACTION introduced by the partial allowlist. It does NOT remove the global winner-per-symbol election underneath it, so bybit_2 can still lose a symbol to a bybit_1-only 5m leg in the divergent case. That is BL-20260827 and it is row E34. [!] MEASURED ON THE LIVE SOAK 2026-09-22 BY THE MANAGER, AND IT PROMOTES THE LANE'S SINGLE ROW TO A POPULATION. Read direct over https://ict-bot.duckdns.org (Transport A, not the relay), log_file?name=arbitration_fanout_soak&lines=400. POPULATION, STATED: 400 rows, 2026-09-14T06:30:57Z -> 2026-09-22T12:05:01Z. Split at 2026-09-22T09:30Z, which is after the allowlist was widened. PRE-FIX (392 rows / 194.9h): 94 rows graded MORE THAN ONE account, and 89 of those 94 show the subtraction — rounds_planned contains accounts that rounds_written does not. BY ACCOUNT, counting how often each was DELETED from a round it had already won: **bybit_2 58, bybit_portfolio 58, breakout_1 57**. The lane established this on ONE row; it is 58 for real money over eight days. It is also the direct mechanism behind the 12/1/1 closed-trade split in this row's lead — same accounts, same window, same direction. Affected symbols: ETHUSDT 47, XRPUSDT 23, SOLUSDT 15, BTCUSDT 9. [!] AND IT CARRIES E17 WITH IT: breakout_1 was deleted 57 times, so 'breakout_1 receives nothing' is the SAME defect seen from the prop side, not a separate one. E17's blocked_on edge naming this row is discharged by the same set-env. [!] ⚠️ POST-FIX THE SAMPLE PROVES NOTHING YET, AND THAT IS WHY THIS ROW IS STILL landed_unproven. 8 rows over 2.2h, 0 of which grade more than one account and 0 of which show a subtraction. THAT ZERO IS NOT EVIDENCE: at the pre-fix rate of 0.482 multi-account rows/hour you would expect ~1.1 in 2.2h, so 0 is the modal outcome of a sample too small to contain the case. A negative needs a denominator and this one does not have one. Every post-fix row is bybit_1-only because bybit_2 simply had no candidate on those ticks (no XRPUSDT row at all in the window, and the two ETHUSDT ticks fired eth_pullback_2h, which is a bybit_1-only leg). [!] THE OBSERVATION THAT CLOSES THIS ROW, NAMED PRECISELY: one soak row logged AFTER 2026-09-22T09:30Z on a symbol where bybit_2 holds a candidate (XRPUSDT, or an ETHUSDT tick on which trend_donchian_eth_4h fires) with rounds_written[].accounts == rounds_planned[].accounts INCLUDING bybit_2 — AND THEN a journal row for bybit_2, because the soak's own docstring says a soak row proves the decision, never the order. Expect the first within ~2-4h of normal trading; re-read the same path. [!] LANE HANDOVER RECORDED 2026-09-22, and the row was WRONG about itself until now: it read `in_flight` against a lane that was not working. its lane FAILED at 10:45Z — 'The model's tool call could not be parsed (retry also failed)' — mid-turn, with its branch pushed. The manager resolved its register conflicts and added the population measurement. The manager has held this row since, so the `lane` field now names the manager rather than a dead session. ⚠️ THIS IS NOT A GOOD OUTCOME AND IS RECORDED AS ONE OF THE FOUR. items.title: Derive the settled-evidence cut-points from the arm's own purpose (expected armings per horizon), not from a picked share
items.note: [!] ID CORRECTED 2026-09-22 by the manager: this row was filed as E42 from a branch cut before #12725 landed, and E42 was taken on main by an unrelated row (the accounts.yaml symbol list). Two rows sharing an id is the collision E13 built a check for one level up, and it would have merged as a silent clobber rather than a conflict. Renamed to E47; no content changed. SPLIT OUT OF E41 BY THE LANE, 2026-09-22, so the flag could land today. The operator REJECTED the two proposed cut-points, verbatim: "we need data-backed values, not arbitrary ones (otherwise what's the point of the arm in the first place?)". PR #12745 lands the flag WITHOUT them -- it emits `settled_*` only where the verdict is invariant across the still-open cut-point band -- and this row is the derivation that closes the gap. [!] THE SPECIFICATION IS THE OPERATOR'S OWN PARENTHESIS. An arm exists to modify exits on trades that REACH arm_r, so the quantity that matters is not a bare share but EXPECTED ARMINGS PER HORIZON at the leg's own trade rate. A 5% reach share is ~10 armings/year on a leg trading 200 times a year and ~0.3 on a leg trading 6 times a year; those are different facts and one share-threshold cannot separate them. That also makes the threshold PER LEG, which is why the current band has to be leg-independent and therefore weak. [!] PROPOSED DERIVATION, written out so this needs no re-deriving. (1) expected_armings(leg, horizon) = reach_share * trades_per_horizon(leg). (2) trades_per_horizon is MEASURABLE TODAY and needs no new instrument: every comms/strategy_evidence/runs/<run>/<leg>__bt.json carries `total_trades` with `data_start` and `data_end`, so trades/day falls straight out; the same files already back the k/n in config/lever_reachability.json. (3) settled_inert when the CI-HIGH share implies FEWER THAN ONE expected arming over the horizon -- i.e. even the optimistic end of the interval predicts the lever never fires in that window. settled_reachable when the CI-LOW implies at least N. (4) [!] THE HORIZON AND N ARE THE PART THAT IS STILL UNDERIVED, AND THEY MUST COME FROM SOMETHING REAL -- the demotion-review cadence, the corpus span, the e35 re-check interval -- with the file saying WHERE EACH CAME FROM. Do not substitute a round number; that is the exact failure this row exists to correct. If the corpus cannot support a derivation, SAY SO and say what would: an honest 'cannot be derived from what we have' beats a second invented pair, and the flag already degrades safely to `unsettled` in that case. [!] WHERE TO WRITE IT: config/lever_reachability.json::evidence_flag_policy, replacing `plausible_cut_band` (or narrowing it) and flipping `status` off UNDERIVED. The grading code is scripts/ops/lever_evidence_flag.py::grade, which already reads the policy from the registry and already stores, per basis, the exact cut-points its own verdict flips at (`settled_reachable_if_reach_cut_at_or_below_pct` / `settled_inert_if_inert_cut_above_pct`) -- those are the inputs a derived threshold gets compared against, so the arithmetic is already laid out. Keep the self-test's non-vacuity control and add one showing a leg's flag MOVING when only its trade rate changes, which is the property this row adds. [!] WHAT THE DERIVATION WILL LIKELY SHOW, recorded in advance so it is falsifiable rather than confirmed after the fact: on the current corpus only uso_trend_1h clears any reachable bar, and NOTHING reaches settled_inert, because the inert side needs a horizon long enough that <1 expected arming is a real statement and the live populations are n=1 to n=37. If the derivation produces a confident `settled_inert` on a single-digit n, that is a sign the horizon was chosen to produce it.

items.title: Fix the arbitration at source: elect PER ACCOUNT off the once-gated set, retire the fan-out workaround
items.note:
OPERATOR DIRECTIVE 2026-09-22: 'we need to fix the fanout mechanism'. [!] THE FAN-OUT IS A WORKAROUND LAYERED ON THE GLOBAL ELECTION, NOT A FIX OF IT, and it says so itself -- src/runtime/pipeline.py:1088: 'Per-account arbitration fan-out ... so an account whose own candidate lost the GLOBAL election is no longer dropped by `pkg.strategy in assigned` and silenced without a journal row.' The global dispatcher picks ONE winner per symbol across all accounts and then fans out; any account whose own candidate lost is dropped silently. The fan-out repairs that damage after the fact. It solves nothing the global dispatcher could not have avoided by not creating the problem. [!] AND THE STATED BLOCKER TO FIXING IT PROPERLY IS ALREADY OBSOLETE -- THIS IS THE FINDING. The reason given for never making the election per-account is that a per-account aggregator would re-emit a `regime_hard_gate` row per account per tick, corrupting the signal that partitions `would have gated` from `did gate`. But intent_multiplexer.py:876 ALREADY SPLITS GATE FROM ELECT, in a comment that says exactly why: 'Gate ONCE, then elect. aggregate_intents is exactly this composition, but spelling it out is what lets the per-account fan-out below elect N times off the SAME gated set without re-emitting a regime_hard_gate row per account per tick.' `_gated, _pre_gate = gate_intents(intents, symbol=symbol)` then `elect_from_gated(_gated, ...)`. THE MACHINERY TO ELECT PER ACCOUNT WITHOUT CORRUPTING THE AUDIT SIGNAL IS IN THE FILE AND IN USE TODAY. The fan-out is the existence proof. [!] THE SHAPE OF THE FIX: call elect_from_gated per account off the one gated set and dispatch the union, instead of electing once globally and scoping a repair round. Then there is no global winner to starve anyone, ARBITRATION_FANOUT_ACCOUNTS becomes unnecessary, and the failure mode measured today -- a partial allowlist SUBTRACTING accounts from rounds they had won -- cannot exist because there is no allowlist. [!] TODAY'S ALL-11 ALLOWLIST IS SCAFFOLDING, NOT A SETTLED DESIGN. It removes the subtraction; it leaves the global election underneath it (BL-20260827) untouched. [!] TIER 3 -- it changes live routing on real-money accounts. Prove it against the same test the E33 lane wrote (tests/test_arbitration_fanout_allowlist_scope.py, which asserts TODAY'S DEFECTIVE BEHAVIOUR on purpose so the fix has to flip it CONSCIOUSLY); flipping those assertions is part of the deliverable and must be visible in the diff.

This row is cheap and its blast radius is the whole corpus. A leg cannot go shadow -> live without the guard calling its record stale, because the flip changes the thing being fingerprinted. B1 landed 2026-09-21 and this is the first promotion attempted since; the defect has been latent for a day and would have blocked every one. [!] THE FIX IS A CORRECTNESS FIX, NOT A WEAKENING: fingerprint the STRATEGY PARAMETERS the backtest measured, excluding `execution` (and almost certainly `enabled`) -- neither is a strategy property and neither changes what a harness would produce. A moved atr_stop_mult, entry_z or lookback must still invalidate the record, and the guard's own self-test at line 626 ('P6 stale config_fingerprint fails identity', plus 'P6 ...while all four clauses still PASS (so identity is load-bearing)') must keep passing so the failure branch stays proven. [!] TWO WRONG FIXES, NAMED SO THEY ARE NOT TAKEN: (a) regenerating the evidence record after the flip -- it re-runs a backtest to account for a gate change that cannot affect the result, and it teaches the next session that the answer to a guard complaint is to re-roll the evidence; (b) wiring the roster WITHOUT the execution flip -- the fingerprint stays valid and the guard passes, and you get a leg that looks promoted and trades nothing, which is the silent-inert failure mode the missing AVAXUSDT symbol nearly produced the same hour. [!] FIXED AND MERGED 2026-09-22 in #12725 (operator: 'Yes push it'). _GATE_FIELDS = {execution, enabled} excluded from the digest in BOTH scripts/ops/build_strategy_evidence.py (the producer) and scripts/ci/check_roster_promotion_evidence.py (the guard, which re-implements rather than imports so CI does not pull the producer's research deps), each carrying a comment that the set must NOT be widened to quiet a complaint. The 52 records were migrated in a way that PRESERVES the staleness signal rather than washing it out: each was graded under the OLD scheme against origin/main:config/strategies.yaml first (NOT the working tree, which carried the branch's own execution flip and would have begged the question), and a record whose parameters had genuinely drifted would have kept its old digest and still read STALE. Result 52 migrated / 0 already-stale kept, and the diff over the records is exactly 52 changed lines, all config_fingerprint. VERIFIED: --self-test PASS including 'P6 stale config_fingerprint fails identity' and 'P6 ...while all four clauses still PASS (so identity is load-bearing)', so the failure branch stays proven; the two implementations agree over all 55 config blocks; and controls confirm a gate flip does NOT move the digest while a moved atr_stop_mult DOES. [!] `landed_unproven` NOT `done`: what closes it is the guard ARMING a promotion on main — which #12725 itself is (`armed: ada_pullback_2h -> bybit_2 [roster_add]`), so this closes with R8's own observation. [2026-09-25 verification sweep] CLOSING OBSERVATION MADE: python3 scripts/ci/check_roster_promotion_evidence.py --self-test -> "self-test: PASS" (incl. "P6 stale config_fingerprint fails identity" and its four-clauses-still-pass companion). The guard's stated closing condition -- the guard arming a promotion on main -- is confirmed trading: /api/bot/trades/closed?account_id=bybit_2&since=2026-09-22T09:30:00Z shows 3 closed ada_pullback_2h trades on bybit_2 (ids 6091/6113/6143, pnlProvenance measured).

items.title: Strip the trail-decay arms that cannot fire under the venue TP cap (operator decision 2026-09-22)
items.note:
[!] OPERATOR DECISIONS 2026-09-22, LATE, AND THEY CHANGE WHAT THIS ROW CLOSES ON. The two proposed settled-evidence cut-points are WITHDRAWN as invented ("we need data-backed values, not arbitrary ones (otherwise what's the point of the arm in the first place?)"); Clopper-Pearson STANDS; #12745 is APPROVED TO LAND carrying the withdrawal rather than the numbers; THIS PR (#12737) is HELD and "don't let it be a blocker". E41 NOW CLOSES ON #12745, NOT ON #12737. [!] #12737 IS CONVERTED BACK TO DRAFT so nothing reads it as ready. What would unhold it: a decision to strip arms we cannot show are dead. Both legs it strips grade `unsettled` -- gld_pullback_1d on 0/8 (exact 95% CI to 36.9%) and qqq_trend_long_1d on 0/1 (to 97.5%) -- and under the flag as landed NO entry can be graded a settled dead arm at all, because the inert side of the cut-point band has no anchor. [!] DONE IN #12745 (head 2e4394705): status -> UNDERIVED, both cut-point fields DELETED (not nulled, so nothing reads them as adopted-but-empty), and grading moved from a point test to INVARIANCE across a `plausible_cut_band` -- a `settled_*` flag is emitted only where the verdict holds for EVERY cut-point still open. The band's reachable edge 88.4% is ANCHORED BY OBSERVATION: uso_trend_1h's lever ARMED AND FIRED in production (pkg-29261c70cb4e41ba), so any cut-point grading it not-reachable is refuted by the firing. The inert edge is NULL because nothing anchors it, and a null edge makes `settled_inert` UNREACHABLE rather than permissive. MEASURED: exactly ONE of eight entries is settled (uso). Self-test 19/19. [!] AND trend_donchian_xrp_4h MOVES settled_reachable -> unsettled, AGAINST THE DISPATCH'S EXPECTATION ('at 35.9% likewise'): its CI low is 35.9 so its verdict flips for any reachable cut-point above that, and its sample is the 6 NEWEST of up to 25 rows, truncated and recency-biased in a way an interval cannot see. Recorded, not resolved by a lane. [!] THE DERIVATION IS NOT DONE AND IS SPLIT TO ROW E42 with the full proposed construction written out (expected armings per horizon at the leg's own trade rate, measurable today from each __bt.json's total_trades and span). This lane was at ~$76 against a ceiling the manager itself said was mis-set, so it filed the derivation rather than half-building it. [!] CI ON #12737 WENT RED AND IT WAS MINE: tests/test_roster_promotion_evidence.py::test_fingerprint_agrees_with_every_committed_record, '4/52 committed records are STALE' -- exactly the four legs the config edit touched. An edge record carries a config_fingerprint so a moved config makes it STALE by design. FIXED by re-running scripts/ops/build_strategy_evidence.py for the two legs the PR still edits (yfinance was absent from the sandbox; installed it). RESULT, and the two legs answer DIFFERENTLY: gld_pullback_1d is BYTE-IDENTICAL on every edge number (net_r_oos 13.6569, n=6) because its record already listed trail_decay_arm_r under `omitted_levers` -- the harness never modelled the arm, so removing it provably cannot move the number. qqq_trend_long_1d MOVED: net_r_oos 1.9389 -> 6.6307, n_trades_oos 7 -> 4, stop-outs 5 -> 2, on an IDENTICAL span with every other param identical. [!] THAT DELTA IS A HARNESS-FIDELITY ARTIFACT AND MUST NOT BE READ AS A BENEFIT OF THE STRIP: both runs carry tp_r: None -- the harness models NO take-profit -- while the live leg's TP fills at min(entry*1.099, entry + 3.0*risk). Live the ceiling is <= 3.0R so the 3.56R arm cannot fire and removing it changes nothing; in the harness MFE runs free, the arm fires, and removing it spares three stop-outs. Filed PI-20260922-E41-0006. [!] AND THE RECORD CLAIMS `fidelity: faithful` with `omitted_levers: []` WHILE OMITTING tp_r -- a false completeness claim on the artifact the M7 gate reads its edge verdict from (PI-20260922-E41-0005). [!] A THIRD DEFECT, OBSERVED: a FAILED producer run overwrites a committed `measured` record with a harness_failed stub -- two real measurements were destroyed and restored only because git diff was read before committing (PI-20260922-E41-0007). [!] SETTLED-EVIDENCE FLAG SHIPPED SEPARATELY, PR #12745 (Tier-1, landing hold). Operator 2026-09-22: 'we can leave the arm for now, we just need a flag for when its results are statistically significant vs. when it shouldn't be considered settled evidence.' Built: scripts/ops/lever_evidence_flag.py computes an exact (Clopper-Pearson) 95% interval and a four-state flag (settled_inert / settled_reachable / unsettled / not_measured, never collapsed) from each basis's k,n, stored in config/lever_reachability.json under an evidence block + evidence_flag_policy; guard lever-evidence-flag-guard; self-test 16/16 with a non-vacuity control. MEASURED over all 8 entries: SIX of eight entry flags are `unsettled` or `not_measured`, including BOTH legs the strip PR #12737 ships -- gld_pullback_1d (0/8, CI upper 36.9%) and qqq_trend_long_1d (0/1, CI upper 97.5%) are `unsettled`, not settled_inert. Chose Clopper-Pearson over the dispatch's Wilson because 95% Wilson calls 1/1 reachable (lower 20.6%) and trend_donchian's only basis is n=1; the two agree on all 9 cells the dispatch tabulated. The two cut-points are PROPOSED and are an operator decision, flagged as such in the file. pr-landing-guard R5 REFUSED the dispatched self-land (config/lever_reachability.json is Tier-2 by path), so it is landing:hold like the strip. OPERATOR DECISION 2026-09-22 (Tier-3): 'strip the arms entirely' -- remove the reach-gate from the legs where it cannot fire, so the config stops declaring a protection that does not exist. CLARIFIED by the operator the same day, verbatim: "I only wanted to strip the arm where it can't produce a result, it should stay where it can produce one." THE TEST IS ZERO, NOT RARE. Finding: BL-20260816-TRAIL-DECAY-ARM-R-SITS-ABOVE-THE-VENUE-TP-CAP; pipeline row BL-20260823-DECLARED-TRAIL-DECAY-ARMS-ARE-INERT-UNDER-THE-VENUE-CAP. [!] WHICH FACT THIS REACHED: NONE OF THE THREE. Not merged, not deployed, not observed. PR #12737 is a DRAFT held for the manager; a Tier-3 config change is not a lane's to land. The only things OBSERVED are the pre-change code and config, cited below. [!] SHIPPED: TWO legs, both measured ZERO. gld_pullback_1d `trail_decay_arm_r: 5.06` -- 0 of 8 live order_packages over the leg's COMPLETE history (cap_R 2.20-3.01), re-checked 2026-09-22 at the unchanged atr_stop_mult 2.0 and reading 0 of 6. qqq_trend_long_1d `trail_decay_arm_r: 3.56` -- cap_R 2.13 on two independent bases agreeing exactly. Both were already verdict=inert / disposition=recorded_inert (operator, 2026-08-16); `inert` is this registry's own word for 'no observed entry could reach the arm', so the clarified test reaches them. They shipped first as a deliberately separable commit and the clarification folded them into scope. [!] NOTHING ELSE WAS CHANGED, AND TWO STRIPS WERE REVERTED INSIDE THIS SESSION BEFORE ANYTHING MERGED. xrp_pullback_2h (4.49) and avax_pullback_2h (4.86) were stripped under the first reading and RESTORED under the clarification: they measure 2/37 (5.4%) and 2/45 (4.4%), which is non-zero, so the operator's test does not reach them and the manager has put the question back. Their arms stand exactly as before. PI-20260922-E41-0004. [!] trend_donchian_sol_4h WAS NAMED FOR STRIPPING IN BOTH THE DISPATCH AND THE CLARIFICATION AND IS STILL HELD -- THIS IS THE MAIN FINDING. Both cite 'LIVE 0/16 (COMPLETE) and backtest 0/127 across every year'. Both were measured 2026-08-16 at atr_stop_mult 2.5. The leg has run 1.5 since 892c9a2c8 (#10450) landed 2026-08-30, and cap_R = 0.099/(risk/entry) scales by 1.667x with it. MEASURED on the geometry the leg runs TODAY: 4 of 34 entry-conditioned backtest trades reach the 5.57R arm (11.8%), cap_R max 6.459, from comms/strategy_evidence/runs/2026-09-22-r5/trend_donchian_sol_4h__trades.jsonl. The clarification's own sentence re-prices: 'the arm needs risk/entry <= 1.777% and the leg's lowest-vol entry EVER observed is 2.292%' becomes 1.375% under the new stop, which CLEARS. Applying the operator's test to a current measurement says do not strip; applying it to the stale one says strip. Only the operator can retire their own evidence. PI-20260922-E41-0001. [!] AND scha_trend_long_1d, cited in BOTH messages as a leg that FIRES (83.1%), NOW LOOKS INERT -- flagged, untouched, as instructed. That figure is the VENUE cap only. M20 B4 (#10419, 2026-08-29) cut its tp_r 50.0 -> 1.5 and atr_stop_mult 2.5 -> 3.0; the placed TP is min(entry*(1+0.099), entry + tp_r*risk), so the ceiling is min(cap_R, 1.5) against a 2.00R arm. PI-20260922-E41-0002. [!] THE CONSUMER QUESTION, ESTABLISHED FROM THE CODE BEFORE EDITING -- removing the key does NOT activate a worse default. src/runtime/trail_decay.py:139-145 reads `arm_r = _f(...) or 0.0` and guards EVERY use with `arm_r > 0`, so 0.0 is an off-sentinel and the R-arm goes inactive. What it DOES change: `declared = tight > 0 and (arm_r > 0 or stall > 0)`, so a leg with no `trail_decay_stall_bars` (qqq) drops to the UNDECLARED branch -- base trail mult returned, identical to today because the arm could not fire, plus one OBSERVE-ONLY exit_lever_soak.jsonl annotate row per package when the reference stall-6 cell would arm. gld keeps `trail_decay_stall_bars: 10`, so its lever stays declared and working. The giveback sibling behaves the same way (src/runtime/exit_levers.py:231-241: an absent `giveback_min_mfe_r` falls to the annotate-only path, never a live close); no giveback lever is touched. [!] CORRECTED A LOAD-BEARING NOTE: config/lever_reachability.json's `basis_note` said the ceiling is cap_R = 0.099/(risk_per_unit/entry). That is the whole ceiling only while `tp_r` is the 50.0 sentinel. Read in code 2026-09-22 at src/units/strategies/trend_donchian.py:393 and htf_pullback_trend_2h.py:351, the placed TP is min(entry*(1+0.099), entry + tp_r*risk), so the ceiling is min(cap_R, tp_r). Four legs acquired a real tp_r after the 2026-08-16 measurements. Third correction to that note, and the reason two of this row's findings exist. [!] MEASUREMENT ADDED THAT DID NOT EXIST: avax_pullback_2h had NO registry row at all (it is `execution: shadow`, so the guard never required one, and the 2026-08-23 audit named it as one of four legs it did not look at). Its 2/45 was computed this session and the probe was validated on legs whose answers are known -- uso_trend_1h 55/55 = 100% matching `reachable`, gld_pullback_1d 0/6 matching `inert`. The row was added so the measurement survives. [!] GUARD: `stripped` added to check_lever_reachability.py's disposition enum with its own self-test case, so the self-test reports 11/11 rather than 10/10 -- a case was ADDED. Real-tree declared reach-gates: 8 before, 6 after. [!] VERIFICATION: check_lever_reachability.py PASS + --self-test 11/11; run_guards.py with GUARDS_BASE_REF=main and the PR diff PASS 57 / FAIL 0; 187 passed / 1 skipped over the exit-lever and strategy test set; pipeline.py --check exit 0. [!] NOT A RISK TO CAPITAL. An inert arm costs one refinement that never fires; the legs still trade their entry, stop and TP unchanged.

[MAIN]
OPERATOR-RAISED 2026-09-22, verbatim: 'are there no decisions waiting for me?' — asked after the manager reported that ZERO rows on this register carried an operator_decision edge. That report was accurate about the field and WRONG about the world, and this row is the correction. [!] THE STRUCTURAL FINDING, WHICH MATTERS MORE THAN ANY ONE ARM. Tier-3 decisions have been accumulating in a DOMAIN register (config/lever_reachability.json) whose `disposition: queued_tier3` state means precisely 'a correction is proposed and awaiting the operator'. Nothing reads that file into the checklist, the brief, or GET /api/bot/work/checklist. Three of the four rows were opened 2026-08-16 and have sat FIVE WEEKS. This is the parking-lot failure CLAUDE.md warns about, in a register the manager added a fifth row to this very session without noticing. [!] AND THREE OF THE FOUR ARE NOT WAITING ON WORK — THEIR MEASUREMENT IS ALREADY TAKEN. Read from the registry 2026-09-22, each figure with its population: trend_donchian_sol_4h arm 5.57 — LIVE entry-conditioned (the AUTHORITATIVE basis, population COMPLETE) 0/16, backtest 0/127 across every year 2023-2026, cap_R median 1.78 live / 1.64 backtest; the arm needs risk/entry <= 1.777% and the leg's BEST (lowest-vol) entry ever observed is 2.292%, so it is not a near-miss, it is out of range — and it is STILL filed `verdict: unmeasured`, because the session that measured it deliberately left every verdict untouched 'for consistency'. A measurement that never became a verdict is the same collapsed state as `0` meaning 'we could not look'. xrp_pullback_2h arm 4.49 — LIVE COMPLETE 2/37 (5.4%), backtest 12/204 (5.9%), cap_R median 3.03; verdict `vol_conditional`, which the legend calls 'a real design choice, not a default' — nobody has made the choice. scha_trend_long_1d arm 2.00 — no live basis obtainable (the leg was declared 2026-08-09 and the live journal holds ZERO order packages for it, a `looked_and_found_nothing` read, not a failure), backtest 54/65 = 83.1%, cap_R median 2.65 ABOVE the arm. This is the one that is probably FINE. avax_pullback_2h arm 4.86 — opened 2026-09-22 by an R8 promotion that was then WITHDRAWN the same session (fold recency, not reachability), so this leg is `execution: shadow` and is NOT in the guard's denominator; the entry is kept because the measurement is real and throwing it away would mean re-deriving it the next time promotion is considered — backtest entry-conditioned 2/45 = 4.4%, stable across both years (2025 1/14, 2026 1/31), cap_R median 3.27; live basis NOT PULLED, which is different from absent and is recorded that way. [!] WHAT AN INERT ARM COSTS, STATED SO THIS IS NOT OVER-SOLD: an exit lever that cannot arm means one REFINEMENT never fires. The leg still trades its entry, its stop and its TP. Nothing is unprotected. The cost is that a declared, Tier-3-approved lever is decoration, and — per BL-20260816-TRAIL-DECAY-ARM-R-SITS-ABOVE-THE-VENUE-TP-CAP, the finding this whole registry exists to stop recurring — an inert lever is indistinguishable from an armed one that has simply not triggered yet. That is the defect, not a risk to capital. [!] MANAGER RECOMMENDATION, one per leg: trend_donchian_sol_4h -> `inert` + `recorded_inert` (the authoritative population is complete and unambiguous; recording it closes the row with no code change and no arm edit). scha_trend_long_1d -> `reachable` + `ok` on the backtest basis, or leave queued if the operator wants a live basis it cannot have for months. avax_pullback_2h and xrp_pullback_2h -> the manager pulls the live order_packages basis FIRST (both are cheap relay reads), then the operator decides on complete information rather than on a backtest proxy. [!] AND THE REGISTER GAP IS ITS OWN DELIVERABLE, SEPARATE FROM THE FOUR ARMS: whatever is decided, `queued_tier3` in a domain register must become visible. Cheapest honest fix is a check that FAILS when any domain register holds an operator-gated row that no checklist row points at — the same shape as the collapsed-state guard, and it would have caught this in August. [!] ⚠️ THE FOURTH ROW'S OWN FRAMING WAS CORRECTED IN PLACE, and the correction is worth keeping: this row was filed while avax_pullback_2h was staged for bybit_2, and the entry's `unmeasured_reason` asserted the promotion as the reason it existed. The promotion was withdrawn hours later. Corrected in config/lever_reachability.json rather than only here, because a wrong claim that merges is the repo's position. [!] OPERATOR DECIDED 2026-09-22, choosing between four options: **STRIP THE ARMS ENTIRELY** — remove the reach-gate parameter from the legs where it CANNOT FIRE, so the config stops declaring a protection that does not exist. Dispatched as a lane the same minute. ⚠️ THE BOUNDARY IS THE WHOLE TASK AND IT IS THE OPERATOR'S OWN WORDING: 'where it cannot fire' EXCLUDES scha_trend_long_1d, whose arm 2.00 measures 54/65 = 83.1% reachable with cap_R median 2.65 ABOVE it. That lever FIRES; stripping it would remove a working protection, which is the opposite of the decision. Also excluded: uso_trend_1h (100%) and trend_donchian (100%), both verdict `reachable`. STRIPPING: trend_donchian_sol_4h 5.57 (live 0/16 COMPLETE, backtest 0/127), xrp_pullback_2h 4.49 (live 2/37 COMPLETE), avax_pullback_2h 4.86 (backtest 2/45; shadow leg, entry kept as a measurement). IN A SEPARATE, TRIVIALLY DROPPABLE COMMIT: gld_pullback_1d 5.06 and qqq_trend_long_1d 3.56, already `inert`/`recorded_inert` — the same 'cannot fire' test applies and stripping them is the follow-through of an adjudication the operator already made, but it is NOT what they were shown when they answered. [!] THE THING MOST LIKELY TO GO WRONG, NAMED IN THE DISPATCH: if a consumer reads the key as `cfg.get("trail_decay_arm_r", <default>)`, REMOVING the key ACTIVATES the default — the opposite of stripping. The lane must establish that from the code before editing, not assume it. [!] LANE CLOSED 2026-09-22, reported and idle at ceiling; row set to landed_unproven and lane cleared so it does not read as live. Closes on #12745 MERGED and `lever_evidence_flag.py --check` passing from main with `evidence_flag_policy.status: underived` and exactly one entry graded settled (uso_trend_1h). The cut-point DERIVATION is not this row — it is E47. #12737 (the arm strip) is HELD and is explicitly NOT a blocker on anything, per the operator.

[!] CLOSED 2026-09-24. Every clause of this row's OWN stated close condition was checked from main at d0a80f0c1, not assumed: #12745 MERGED; `lever_evidence_flag.py --check` EXIT 0 ('every stored share, interval and flag reproduces from its own k/n under the registry's declared policy'); `evidence_flag_policy.status` UNDERIVED with both proposed cut-points DELETED; exactly ONE of 9 entries graded settled, and it is uso_trend_1h. The cut-point derivation remains E47's, not this row's.
[!] AND #12737 LANDED TOO, which this row said it did not close on. Tier-3, merged deliberately on the operator's 'Land it - resolve and merge'. Verified by reading the FIELD, not the prose: gld's 5.06 and qqq's 3.56 now appear in config/strategies.yaml only inside the removal comment and the ROLLBACK line, and active `trail_decay_arm_r` declarations read 6 -- matching the PR's predicted 8 -> 6. xrp 4.49 and avax 4.86 stand untouched, as decided.
[!] THE EVIDENCE CORPUS WAS REGENERATED BY THE HARNESS, NOT HAND-EDITED. The fingerprint test failed 2/52 STALE on exactly the two stripped legs; build_strategy_evidence.py was re-run; its first attempt returned harness_failed and E46's protection REFUSED to overwrite the committed measured records (working as designed -- missing yfinance, and GLD/QQQ are the Yahoo lane). After installing it: both `measured`, 0 stale, 60 tests pass, runs/2026-09-24/ committed with them.
  qqq_trend_long_1d  n 7 -> 5  net_r_oos 1.9389 -> 6.5977
  gld_pullback_1d    n 6 -> 5  net_r_oos 13.6569 -> 13.8945  (omitted_levers correctly drops the arm)
[!] QQQ'S +246% IS THE KNOWN ARTIFACT, MEASURED THIS TIME RATHER THAN INFERRED. PI-20260922-E41-0006 called it two days earlier; the manager re-derived it without checking and briefly reported it as new, which was the error. What is added is a CONTROL: same harness, same day, only the arm toggled -> arm ON n=8 net_r_oos=1.9059, arm OFF n=5 net_r_oos=6.5977, and the arm-ON run's first SEVEN per-trade rows are byte-identical to runs/2026-09-22-r5 (1.9389 + -0.033 = 1.9059, exact). So r5 REPRODUCES, the branch's rejected numbers were never corroborated, and the whole move is the config change. Graded continuation: PI-20260924-JN54P2HH-0005 (tier 2, high) -- -0005/-0006/-0007 had all sat queued with tier=None and severity=None since 2026-09-22.

[!] DEPLOYED AND OBSERVED 2026-09-24T11:18Z — the three facts are now separate and all three are established. Dispatched pull-and-deploy (#12825) on the operator's Tier-2 OK in chat ('Approve - one batched deploy + verify'), with the expected post-state REGISTERED IN THE DISPATCH BEFORE THE RUN. Measured from GET /api/bot/runtime-config, pre vs post:

[!] THIS ALSO RETIRES A TIMING INFERENCE RATHER THAN LEAVING IT STANDING. Before the deploy the manager read git_sha 0d00987f4 (which contains E42 and E17) against a 10:16:49Z boot and inferred both were already live. That inference was probably right and was NOT an observation -- git_sha reports the WORKING TREE, not the code the process loaded. The operator was told the opposite of it in an approval popup ('NONE of them is on the live VM'), which was wrong; corrected in chat and recorded here. The 11:18:11Z boot post-dates all three merges, so the question is now settled by measurement instead of by argument.

[!] ⚠️ THREE OPERATOR DECISIONS THIS ROW CARRIED ARE STILL OPEN, AND CLEARING `blocked_on` TO CLOSE THE ROW REMOVED THEIR MACHINE-READABLE EDGE. Said plainly because the row now reads `done` and three of its four edges were never about #12737 at all:
  · PI-20260922-E41-0001  trend_donchian_sol_4h — strip HELD. Its 0/16 + 0/127 zeros were measured at atr_stop_mult 2.5; the leg has run 1.5 since 2026-08-30 and re-measures 4/34 (11.8%). Only the operator can retire their own evidence.
  · PI-20260922-E41-0004  xrp_pullback_2h (2/37, on bybit_2 REAL MONEY) + avax_pullback_2h (2/45) — non-zero, so the operator's zero test does not reach them; stripping would make a design choice by deletion.
  · PI-20260922-E41-0002  scha_trend_long_1d — cited in both operator messages as a leg that FIRES (83.1%), but that is the venue cap only and its tp_r is now 1.5 against a 2.00R arm. Stale in the DANGEROUS direction.

items.title: accounts.yaml::symbols is a DATA-PULL list, not a gate — the roster is the single source for what trades, and a stale pull list is a pull-list bug, never a trading decision
items.note:
OPERATOR-RAISED 2026-09-22, verbatim: 'In general, I don't get why uh, th there shouldn't be a symbol specific list for each account. That's what the strategy roster is for. It trades whatever the strategies that it's trading are trading... That's exactly the kind of double gate that just stops things from working for no reason that is completely unnecessary to anything that we're doing here.' [!] VERIFIED, AND THE OPERATOR IS RIGHT ON BOTH HALVES — it is a gate, and it is redundant. IT IS A GATE, established in code and not inferred: src/main.py:714 `_resolve_tick_symbols` builds the set of symbols the trader FETCHES CANDLES FOR from each account's `symbols:` list, NOT from its roster. A symbol absent there means no data, no signal, no order — the leg sits on the roster looking wired and trades nothing. Two other readers exist and neither is a gate: src/runtime/intents.py::supported_symbols() unions the declared symbols with a static base as a VALIDATION whitelist and fails SAFE (a config-load failure falls back to the base, never narrower), and intent_multiplexer.py:485 reads the per-STRATEGY symbols, a different field. ⚠️ intents.py:100 contradicts itself inside one sentence — 'This is a validation whitelist, not a runtime on/off gate — accounts.yaml `symbols` drives what actually trades.' Field beats comment, and here the field is main.py:714. IT IS REDUNDANT, MEASURED over all 11 accounts by parsing config/accounts.yaml and config/strategies.yaml 2026-09-22: 19 ORPHAN symbols declared that no rostered leg needs (alpaca_live 8, alpaca_portfolio 7, bybit_2 1, bybit_portfolio 1, ib_live 1, oanda_practice 1), and 0 MISSING. ⚠️ READ THE ZERO CORRECTLY — IT IS NOT REASSURANCE, IT IS THE NEAR-MISS. It reads 0 only because the R8 promotion checked symbol coverage BEFORE the edit: avax_pullback_2h was about to join bybit_2 (REAL MONEY) while AVAXUSDT was absent from its list. Caught by looking, not by any guard — nothing in CI asserts the relationship, so the next one is caught by noticing silence, which is exactly how this class of defect is normally found: late. [!] AND THE FIX IS ALREADY HALF-WRITTEN IN THE SAME FILE: src/main.py:267 `_symbols_for_account` ALREADY derives the union of an account's roster symbols — it simply is not what _resolve_tick_symbols consults. [!] PROPOSED (Tier-2, additive, cannot narrow): _resolve_tick_symbols unions the roster-implied symbols into the declared ones, so the ROSTER is the single source and `symbols:` degrades to an additive override for anything a roster cannot imply. Nothing that trades today stops trading — the change can only ADD symbols to the fetch set. Plus a CI check that a rostered leg's symbol is always reachable, so the AVAXUSDT case fails a build instead of failing quietly. [!] THIS IS NOT THE 'no third gate' RULE BEING RESTATED — IT IS AN INSTANCE OF IT. CLAUDE.md § 'The two execution gates' says 'never hide a capability behind a default-off flag (the pattern that stranded MES)'. A symbol list that must be edited in a second place to let a rostered leg trade is that pattern wearing different clothes, and it stranded a leg today. [!] OPERATOR REFRAMED IT 2026-09-22 AND THE REFRAME IS SHARPER THAN THIS ROW WAS, verbatim: 'There are two separate issues here. There's the issue of what trades on what account and what data gets pulled from the account, and those are two separate things that aren't dependent. Obviously anything that's trading will need to be pulling the data, but we can still continue pulling data... for other things even if they're not being traded. But that shouldn't be formatted as a gate. That should just be formatted as additional data pulls unrelated to the strategies themselves. So we do need to find a way to union that so that we're not doing double declarations. But it also needs to make sure that the data-pull roster is not going to interfere with the strategy roster. And even if something is for some reason missing from the pull list, it doesn't mean that it shouldn't be traded — it means that the pull list is not updated correctly.' [!] SO THE SPEC IS FOUR PROPERTIES, not 'remove the second list': (1) the STRATEGY ROSTER decides what trades, full stop; (2) `symbols:` becomes a pure ADDITIVE data-pull list and it is LEGITIMATE for it to carry symbols nothing trades; (3) fetch set = UNION(roster-implied, declared), so no double declaration; (4) a symbol missing from the pull list is a PULL-LIST BUG, never a reason a rostered leg does not trade — and the CI check's FAILURE MESSAGE must say that, in those terms. [!] THIS CHANGES THE DISPOSITION OF THE 19 ORPHANS: under the reframe they are LEGITIMATE data pulls, not drift to clean up. The lane is fenced off them. My earlier framing called them redundancy; that was the one-list reading and the operator's two-concern reading is better. Dispatched as a lane, Tier-2, landing hold.  ||| LANE REPORT 2026-09-22 (session_01PDnYMJCPBohXArAKpUceZm, Tier-2, HELD). REACHED: merged=NO, deployed=NO, observed=NO. STATE IS `blocked`, NOT `landed_unproven` -- close-out check 3 caught this row asserting `landed_unproven` while the PR was still open. Per the states vocabulary `landed_unproven` means MERGED with the effect unobserved; nothing of this lane is on main. It becomes `landed_unproven` on merge and `done` only on the observation named at the end of this note. Draft PR #12736 open (branch lane/e42-roster-symbol-union), landing hold, hold_reason tier_2_3_needs_approval. RE-VERIFIED RATHER THAN INHERITED (RULE ONE), all four dispatch claims: (a) src/main.py::_resolve_tick_symbols does build the fetch set from acct.symbols and never from the roster - CONFIRMED by reading the function; (b) _symbols_for_account already derives the roster union and had exactly one caller, _apply_per_account_leverage - CONFIRMED by grep (2 call sites, one a test); (c) routing does NOT consult symbols - CONFIRMED: coordinator._dispatch_exclusion_reason tests `pkg.strategy not in assigned` plus symbol->exchange, and the only other account-level `symbols` readers are data pulls (clients.py position cross-check, runtime/exchange_accounts.py fill sweep), which is the operator's framing already true in code; (d) THE ONE DISPATCH CLAIM THAT DID NOT SURVIVE: intents.py::supported_symbols() was described as 'NOT a gate - do not fix it'. It fails safe against a config-load FAILURE, but for a symbol declared on NO account it is a hard refusal - StrategyIntent.__post_init__ RAISES ValueError. It was merely UNREACHABLE, because nothing fetched such a symbol. Widening the fetch set is exactly what makes it reachable, so widening only main.py would have converted a silent no-trade into a ValueError on the live tick path. Both are widened, in the same PR, with a negative control asserting a typo is still refused. PROPERTY PROVEN, NOT ASSERTED: MEASURED over config/accounts.yaml x config/strategies.yaml at 06914ce2f (11 accounts, 9 rostering, 55 strategies) the global fetch set is 23 symbols BEFORE and the same 23 AFTER (0 added, 0 removed), and supported_symbols() is 24 before and 24 after. tests/test_roster_symbol_union.py::TestLiveConfigIsUnchangedByThisPR pins that over the checked-in config so a future edit breaks a test instead of a deploy. GUARD: scripts/ci/check_roster_symbol_reachability.py, registered in run_guards.py as `roster-symbol-reachability`, --self-test run before the tree check on every invocation. 10 controls: the planted 2026-09-22 positive (real-money account rostering avax_pullback_2h while AVAXUSDT is absent from its pull list) goes red; a correct pull list, an orphan-carrying pull list, an empty roster, and an unreadable instruments.yaml all stay green. Its failure message names the PULL LIST and says in terms that the leg trades regardless and that a roster must not be touched to satisfy it. Green on the tree: 0 unreachable. FIELD NOT RENAMED, and the choice was ESTABLISHED not guessed: bot_config.py::_ACCOUNT_PUBLIC_FIELDS publishes `symbols` on /api/bot/config and its own comment says the SPA derives its symbol selectors from it, so a rename breaks a consumer in another repo. Documented instead, in the most-read place (a header block in accounts.yaml) plus 7 other prose surfaces. Both are right about different sets; neither number means anything without the set, so the guard prints its denominators. THE AVAXUSDT NEAR-MISS IS REAL AND NOW HAS A LOCATOR: commit d257fe576 on claude/r8-wire-fold-consistent-legs - STAGED, NOT merged to main - adds avax_pullback_2h to bybit_2's real-money roster and AVAXUSDT to its `symbols:` in the same diff, with an inline comment saying the symbol 'was absent here'. DOC RECONCILIATION (this change makes standing prose false): Prime Directive rule 6 in docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md, root CLAUDE.md, intents.py's self-contradicting comment, bot_config.py, docs/reference/bot-api-reference.md, docs/claude/system-actions.md, docs/TRADE-PIPELINE.md, and three accounts.yaml blocks - one of which had already been corrected once in the OPPOSITE direction and is now dated on both. WHAT WOULD CLOSE THIS ROW (landed_unproven -> done): the operator approves and the change deploys, then /api/diag/ or the trader journal shows a tick fetching a symbol that is roster-implied. Today no such symbol exists (0 missing), so the honest closing observation is the NEXT roster promotion that adds a leg without a pull-list edit: it trades, and roster-symbol-reachability reports the pull list as stale. NOT DONE, DELIBERATELY: accounts with an explicit `strategies: []` (ib_live, oanda_practice) are still skipped entirely, so their 2 declared symbols are still not fetched. Under the operator's 'additive data pulls unrelated to the strategies' framing arguably they should be; changing it would ADD symbols to the live fetch set, which is a behaviour change this lane was not asked for. Filed for the operator rather than decided here. VALIDATION RUN BEFORE OPENING THE PR, not after: scripts/ci/run_guards.py --all on the committed tree = 76 guards PASS / 0 FAIL (roster-symbol-reachability among them); pytest -k 'symbol or intent or account' = 1513 passed / 7 skipped; scripts/ops/pipeline.py --check exit 0 apart from 3 pre-existing grandfathered id collisions; check_canonical_doc_coherence.py passes after the CLAUDE.md + CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md edits. NOT SUBSCRIBED to the PR, per the dispatch instruction for this lane.  ||| OPERATOR DECISION 2026-09-22, relayed by the manager: HOLD #12736; THE SHARED RESOLVER LANDS FIRST, THEN THE UNION. Operator's words: 'we need to serialize the steps so that [the promoted leg] goes live first and isn't stranded on the fix being built and implemented.' The reason is this lane's own finding (a): the union is what turns a stale pull list from 'the leg does not trade' into 'the leg TRADES while the naked-position cross-check cannot see it', and the operator declined that window even transiently. ||| THE LANE'S ROW NOW SPANS FOUR PRs, in landing order: (1) #12744 Tier-1 SELF-LAND — the roster-symbol-reachability guard, split out of #12736. WHY: the operator's standing rule for the hold window is 'any leg promoted while the union is held MUST declare its symbol in the same PR', declared enforced by this guard — and the guard was NOT ON MAIN, it existed only inside the held PR, so during exactly the window it covers it protected nothing (verified with git cat-file against origin/main). Its message now READS src/main.py's AST and says the pre-union truth (the leg does NOT trade) until the union lands, then inverts itself. The first version asserted the union was live while it sat unmerged — field-beats-comment committed inside the instrument built to prevent it. (2) #12746 Tier-1 HELD — the accounts.yaml `mode:` header. Finding (c) plus a SECOND false claim this lane found on re-reading: 'There is no strategy-level toggle' denies `execution: live|shadow`, one of the two declared execution gates (bc8ce1aaa/#1862, 105 declarations, enforced at coordinator.py:1371). Held not by choice: pr-landing-guard R5 refuses self-land on config/accounts.yaml and the refusal is correct, so `unvouchable_paths`. (3) the shared resolver, Tier-2 HELD — src/config/symbol_sets.py, ONE definition replacing FIVE private derivations. Four were known; the FIFTH (account_ib_venue_session) was found by the bypass control in the resolver's own self-test, not by reading. The tick is pinned to mode=DECLARED so it is behaviour-preserving, and flipping that one argument is the whole of #12736. The three data readers move to UNION now — that is the point of the ordering. (4) #12736 Tier-2 HELD — the union, unchanged, waiting on (3). ||| THE RESOLVER'S SAFETY CLAIM, MEASURED not asserted: DECLARED == UNION on all 11 accounts, asserted in the self-test OVER THE REAL CONFIG so the day they diverge is a CI failure rather than a surprise; and the tick's old derivation was reproduced exactly, per account and globally (23 symbols, identical). 21 self-test controls, 2312 tests green, ruff clean under CI's pinned 0.15.x. ||| TWO PRE-EXISTING DECISIONS THIS LANE ALMOST UNDID, both caught by tests rather than by care: MI-222's `TestRosterCrossCheckAlreadyExists` pins that a caller CANNOT switch the Bybit position cross-check off with an empty roster (so `symbols: []` must fall through to accounts.yaml — the resolver's truthiness check is deliberate, not sloppy); and the first draft silently widened a caller's explicit `symbols=[...]` with facts from a file it never named. Four tests caught that and they were right to. ||| ALSO FOUND, FILED, NOT FIXED: check_allow_degraded.py is UNSATISFIABLE since the reset — it resolves ids against `docs/claude/*backlog*.json`, which the 2026-09-21 reset archived, so that glob returns []. No new `# allow-degraded:` annotation can be written anywhere. It presents as four ordinary findings against your own new code with a remedy nobody can perform. PI-20260922-ALLOW-DEGRADED-GUARD-IS-UNSATISFIABLE-...  ||| #12748 IS THE RESOLVER PR NUMBER (this row previously said 'resolver PR (this branch)'). ||| VERIFIED AGAINST MERGED MAIN 2026-09-22 AFTER #12725 LANDED, rather than taken from the dispatch: the ada_pullback_2h promotion to bybit_2 (REAL MONEY) is SAFE on the standing rule — bybit_2's roster is [xrp_pullback_2h, trend_donchian_eth_4h, trend_donchian_xrp_4h, ada_pullback_2h] and its symbols: declares ADAUSDT, so the leg gets candles today even with the union still held. Related: PI-20260923-JN54P2HH-0001 -- the hourly sweep that should have read this ceiling mid-flight fires into an ATTENDED session, so all 25 of its firings queued behind a human instead of running. resolution_criteria UNCHANGED and still unmet on the merge: the mechanism must be ON MAIN and a BLOCKED or over-idle lane must appear on the operator's Workflow page without a manager having run anything. severity: high. --- ORIGINAL DISPATCH NOTE BELOW, kept verbatim as the record --- OPERATOR-DIRECTED 2026-09-22. Asked what to do about the blocked lane E20 found, the operator chose archive-everything-dead 'plus a mechanism to prevent this from continuing to happen'. The archiving is DONE (see below); this row is the mechanism, and it exists because the obvious mechanism was already built, tried, and measured NOT WORKING. [!] WHAT THE SWEEP ACTUALLY COST, measured by the manager 2026-09-22T13:35Z over the 60 most recent sessions on this account (list_sessions mine=true), cost from external_metadata.usage.cost_usd, present on 51 of 60: $6,193.20 total. Buckets: COMPLETED 43 / WORKING 6 / BLOCKED 5 / REVIEW_READY 4 / FAILED 2. The manager archived the dead ones under the operator's instruction: 24 attempted, 24 ARCHIVED, $3,553.06 — 18 on the first call and 6 only after a retry, because the session-tool permission classifier refused them the first time (a 25th, the E34 review lane at $21.95, was deliberately NOT attempted: its PR may still be in flight). Archiving is reversible via unarchive_session, which is why a wrong call here is recoverable and a deletion would not have been. Arithmetic closes: 3,553.06 + 21.95 = 3,575.01, the full candidate set. Largest single line: session_01XYu2vvg9Qgxoqf4jJQyd8i (MI-305), BLOCKED and idle 73.3 hours, $1,343.06, 447M cache-read tokens, ZERO commits — archived. Second: a REVIEW_READY research lane at $736.15 idle 85 hours whose output nobody ever collected. [!] THE MECHANISM MUST NOT BE A PERSON'S MEMORY, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE DIFFICULTY. E20 measured three designs dead before proposing a fourth: (1) a CI guard on git commit recency — killed, because 5 of the 7 WORKING lanes had never committed anything, so it would red five healthy lanes; (2) a CI guard on the offline half — killed, because it fails a contributor's PR over the MANAGER's behaviour, the one actor who cannot fix it; (3) a Routine firing a FRESH session — built, fired once, DISABLED the same minute, because the fired session had no repo checkout (sources: []) and no Claude Code Remote MCP tools, so it could neither read lane_reconcile.py nor call list_sessions. A watcher that cannot reach its subject and reports nothing is the exact defect class this row is about. [!] THE FOURTH DESIGN, AND WHY IT IS DIFFERENT: a PERSISTENT supervisor session created with the repo as a source, woken by a cron Routine bound to it via persistent_session_id. A persistent-session Routine delivers into a session that already HAS a checkout and its own tool grants, which is precisely what the fresh-session firing lacked. ⚠️ THIS IS A HYPOTHESIS UNTIL THE LANE MEASURES IT — E20's three capability checks (a repo checkout present, list_sessions callable, the served model) must be run against the woken supervisor and REPORTED, and if any is absent the design is killed like the other three rather than shipped hopeful. A fallback that is honest beats a watchdog that reports nothing. [!] WHAT IT MAY AND MAY NOT DO, because an autonomous archiver is a way to destroy work: archive only sessions whose bucket is COMPLETED or FAILED AND which are idle beyond a stated threshold AND which hold no open PR — never WORKING, never BLOCKED. A BLOCKED lane is NOT archived: only a human can clear a permission prompt, so the supervisor's job there is to RAISE it fast, and the surface it raises on must be one the operator already reads — the checklist rendered at GET /api/bot/work/checklist — not a chat message and not a new register. Archiving is reversible (unarchive_session); deleting is not, and this row authorises no deletion. resolution_criteria: a supervisor session and its Routine exist; a firing has been OBSERVED to read the repo and call list_sessions (or the design is recorded dead with the reading that killed it); a BLOCKED or over-idle lane appears on the operator's Workflow page without a manager having run anything. severity: high — this is the single largest measured waste in the account and it recurs weekly. [!] DISPATCHED 2026-09-22T13:55Z to session_01VsAt1BzrdspLn6hDzFTGh2 on opus-5 — chosen because the lane's first act is a capability MEASUREMENT whose negative result must be trusted enough to kill the design, and three prior designs were killed on exactly such readings. The dispatch fences it off every WORKING lane and off config/src/deploy, and tells it in terms that an honest 'this cannot be built from a session' is an acceptable outcome. [!] THE FIVE E44 FINDINGS NO LONGER DEPEND ON #12752 LANDING. They existed only in the PIPELINE.jsonl on claude/e44-lane-supervisor-build, and nothing reads a branch -- measured 2026-09-23, each returned 1 on the branch and 0 on main while that PR sat `dirty`. Imported verbatim onto main via #12789: PI-20260922-HDZFTGH2-0001 (the canonical doc still binding every session to an archived coordination board -- UNRELATED to E44 and the most valuable of the five), -0002, -0003 (closed there with the cold-test observation that answered it), PI-20260923-HDZFTGH2-0001 and -0002. The CODE, the mandate and the guard are still only on that branch; only the FINDINGS were rescued.

[!] WITHDRAWN 2026-09-24 — THE 'ONLY A HUMAN CAN CLEAR IT' CLAIM ABOVE IS FALSE AND WAS NEVER TESTED. It is left in place rather than deleted so the correction is legible against what it corrects. FALSIFIED by one attempt: interrupt_session on the walled lane, then a message delivered through a create_trigger with persistent_session_id set to it. MEASURED on session_017mdYduTwtyVPXU54wqNHJx, which had shown no activity for 39 hours (last 2026-09-22T13:51:41Z): the trigger fired 2026-09-24T05:32:00Z and get_session shows a turn at 05:32:42Z ending status_bucket COMPLETED, reporting a clean tree, nothing staged or unpushed, and that its own staged_files:true flag was a FALSE ALARM. The operator's words, recorded because the correction is theirs: 'you can definitely take care of those permissions instead of me'.
[!] AND THE NARROWER FORM, because over-claiming the correction would repeat the original error in the other direction: ONE case establishes this, not two. The same technique was also aimed at session_01R9WFrBK1sbBcpTYgBmvG1q and it did reply, but that session runs a 6-hourly cron that would have woken it anyway, and its own 06:44Z heartbeat states it 'was not itself blocked on anything at the time'. A session that was going to wake regardless is not evidence that a message clears a wall. What is established: a message CAN move a session reporting BLOCKED. What is NOT established: that it always can, or what distinguishes the cases. Do not read this as a guarantee; read it as a probe that must be RUN rather than assumed either way — the original defect was asserting the limit for two days without ever attempting it once.

items.title: Eight CI guards grade NOTHING and eleven more are silently narrowed — and three of the dead are named in the #1 doc as live enforcing mechanisms
items.note: MEASURED by the E20 lane 2026-09-22 over a STATED POPULATION of 95 guard scripts — scripts/ci/check_*.py PLUS scripts/check_*.py, because check_claim_basis.py, the one CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL leans on hardest, lives in the latter. Every module-level repo-path constant tested with `git cat-file -e HEAD:<path>`. Four states, never collapsed: live 30 · degraded 11 · DEAD 8 · no_declared_subject 46 (the instrument cannot speak to those, and it is the LARGEST bucket, so folding it into `live` would be this tool committing the defect it exists to find). [!] THE EIGHT DEAD: check_backlog_unresolve, check_claim_basis, check_open_items, check_operator_owed, check_recurrence_ledger, check_register_field_loss, check_soak_registered, check_stated_population. Every one is the 2026-09-21 reset's blast radius — it archived the four review backlogs, OPEN-ITEMS.json, the lease, SESSIONS.json, MERGE-QUEUE.json, session-board.json, RECURRENCE-LEDGER.json and operator-owed-register.json, and nothing swept the guards that read them. [!] AND THREE ARE NAMED IN docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md AS LIVE MECHANISMS, which is why this is not housekeeping: § Backlog governance says the status enum is 'enforced whole-file over every review backlog by claim-basis-guard'; § 'A soak must carry its own alarm' says check_soak_registered fails when a *_soak.jsonl exists with no register alarm; § Session-end reconciliation says operator-owed-guard fails on an item carried across commits without a state change. All three subjects are archived. A canonical doc naming a mechanism that cannot run is the folklore failure that document has its own section about. [!] OPERATOR DECISION 2026-09-22: RE-POINT THE THREE NAMED ONES, RETIRE THE OTHER FIVE with stated reasons, and correct the doc text to match — the doc follows the decision, it does not lead it. [!] DO NOT PROMOTE THE 19 INTO A HARD FAILURE as part of this. E20 already wired scripts/ci/check_guard_liveness.py REPORT-FIRST, with a dated shrink-only baseline and counts printed every run; only a NEW dead or degraded guard fails. Keep that shape and let the baseline shrink by eight. resolution_criteria: the three re-pointed guards each FAIL on a planted violation against their new subject (a green re-point proves nothing); the five retirements each carry a written reason; CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL no longer claims a mechanism that cannot run; and check_guard_liveness's baseline is smaller by eight with the count visible in the diff. [!] CLOSED 2026-09-22 — PR #12756 MERGED, and `done` rather than `landed_unproven` because all four resolution criteria were RE-CHECKED ON MAIN after the merge (main 8a0669284), not inferred from the merge: (1) the re-pointed guards each FAIL on a violation planted against their new subject — self-tests 11/16/14/11 controls, run on main; (2) the four retired scripts are absent from the tree and each carries its reason in docs/archive/2026-09-21-operating-reset/guards/RETIRED-GUARDS-2026-09-22.md; (3) the only surviving mentions of the archived registers in CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL are inside the dated correction notes (lines 640, 1683), i.e. history, not a live mechanism claim; (4) guard-liveness reads dead 0, baseline 11 of 11, exit 0. [!] FOUR guards were re-pointed, not three: a manager addendum added check_allow_degraded, which was UNSATISFIABLE — 0 of 753 open PIPELINE rows were citable because check_backlog_refs.REF does not match a PI- id at all. [!] AND THE FIFTH RETIREMENT DID NOT HAPPEN: check_stated_population is NOT dead (verified by running it against a planted diff, exit 1); its population is a glob the liveness instrument cannot see, so 1 of 8 dead verdicts (12.5%) was a false positive. items.title: A failed build_strategy_evidence.py run OVERWRITES a committed MEASURED record with a harness_failed stub — two real measurements were nearly lost
items.note: OBSERVED by the E41 lane 2026-09-22, not inferred: its first run of scripts/ops/build_strategy_evidence.py DESTROYED the committed `measured` records for gld_pullback_1d and qqq_trend_long_1d, nulling net_r_oos, n_trades_oos and fold_detail and replacing them with a harness_failed stub. The cause was mundane — yfinance was absent from the sandbox — and that is the point: an ordinary environment gap silently converts evidence into a stub. THEY SURVIVED ONLY BECAUSE THE LANE READ `git diff` BEFORE COMMITTING. On a different day that is two measurements gone, with the commit looking like a routine regeneration. [!] WHY THIS IS MORE THAN A SCRIPT BUG: comms/strategy_evidence/ IS the corpus B1's four-clause bar reads to decide whether a leg may reach a real-money roster, and a harness_failed stub does not read as a loss — it reads as a leg that was never measured. That is the collapsed state this repo files bugs about (`we could not look` rendered identically to `we looked and found nothing`), sitting on the promotion path. [!] THE FIX IS SMALL AND THE SHAPE IS NOT NEGOTIABLE: a failed run must never overwrite a record that currently reads `measured`. Write the failure somewhere it is visible (a separate field, a refusal, a non-zero exit) but leave the measurement intact, and make the refusal LOUD rather than a silent skip. Whether a re-measure may overwrite a measured record when it SUCCEEDS is a different question and stays as it is. [!] AND TWO SIBLINGS FILED BY THE SAME LANE BELONG WITH IT, because they are the same artifact lying about itself: PI-20260922-E41-0005 — qqq's record claims `fidelity: faithful` with `omitted_levers: []` while its harness run omits tp_r entirely, and the README defines faithful as 'modelled EVERY lever the leg's config declares'. Not cosmetic: the omitted lever is the one that moved that leg's number 3.4x (net_r_oos 1.9389 -> 6.6307 on an identical data span, the ONLY difference being arm 3.56 -> 0.0). PI-20260922-E41-0006 carries a prediction registered IN ADVANCE — re-run with tp_r modelled and the two should agree; if they do not, the inert-by-construction reasoning behind the qqq arm strip is wrong and #12737 needs re-opening. resolution_criteria: a planted harness failure against a committed measured record leaves the record BYTE-IDENTICAL and exits non-zero; the fidelity claim is computed from what the run actually modelled rather than asserted; and 0006's prediction is either confirmed or recorded as refuted. items.title: A register-only change should not cost a PR, three landing files and two 20-minute CI cycles
items.note:
OPERATOR-RAISED 2026-09-24, verbatim: 'it just doesn't seem like we've basically spent 24 hours trying to close up something that we were supposed to close up two days ago already... It seems. Like something might be wrong here.' They then chose 'file it as a checklist row' over raising it at the sync.
MEASURED ON ONE REAL CHANGE (#12828, 2026-09-24): flipping TWO fields in MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json from `in_flight`/`blocked` to `done` required a PR, `.github/pr-landing/<slug>.json`, `.github/pr-automerge-requests/<slug>.txt`, `.github/merge-slots/<slug>.json`, and TWO full CI cycles. `pytest-run` is ~20 minutes and every push restarts it. Wall clock from PR open (11:24:15Z) to merge (11:52Z) was 28 minutes for a 35-line docs diff.
⚠️ SPLIT THE CAUSE HONESTLY, because most of it was the manager and a fix aimed at the wrong half will not help. Roughly 40 minutes was MY error: I discovered the landing requirements by failing CI twice instead of running `python3 scripts/ci/check_pr_landing.py --base origin/main`, which takes 8 SECONDS and names every missing file at once. That is a discipline problem, addressed in the handoff, NOT something to build around. What remains after removing it is still real: three landing files and a full test suite for a docs-only diff.
CANDIDATE DIRECTIONS, none decided:
  (a) a docs-only CI path that skips `pytest-run` when the diff touches no Python -- note `guards` must       still run, since pr-landing-guard and the register guards live there;
  (b) let the manager batch register updates into ONE PR per day instead of one per closure;
  (c) collapse the three landing files into one, or derive the merge-slot claim from the declaration.
[!] A CHEAP, SEPARABLE FIX WORTH DOING WHATEVER ELSE IS CHOSEN: pr-landing-guard's R13 failure message tells you to write `docs/claude/session-board.json`, which the 2026-09-21 operating reset ARCHIVED and which CLAUDE.md says not to resurrect. The route that works is `.github/merge-slots/<branch>.json` (MI-280, 2026-09-12), documented ~20 lines below the stale remedy in the guard's own source. That message cost a CI cycle on 2026-09-24 and will cost the next session one too. guard-liveness already baselines check_pr_landing.py as DEGRADED with session-board.json among its absent subjects, so the repo knows the subject is gone -- what nobody noticed is that the REMEDY TEXT still points at it.
[!] NOT ESTABLISHED: whether `pytest-run` can be skipped safely for a docs-only diff. Nobody has checked what in that suite reads docs/ or the registers -- `check_manager_checklist_vocabulary` and `pipeline --check` both do, and both live in `guards`, not `pytest-run`. Establish it before building (a).

items.title: Add prop-roster legs so each prop book cannot breach an inactivity rule and its pass probability rises (tradeify_1 first, then velotrade_1)
items.note: [2026-10-05T11:12Z manager session_01MM8o5js6TcDFeNAPBY4Ntv] OPERATOR (verbatim): 'we also need to prioritize adding more strategies to make sure we can stay within active trading restrictions'. Priority 1 prop. MEASURED by the manager: the Tradeify 1-Step inactivity rule is a breach after 30 consecutive days with no trade; Velotrade needs one trade >=60s per 30 days plus 5 qualifying days; Breakout has no minimum. Over the 730d backtest (n=355 entries) the single ETH leg's max gap between entries is 7.5d (median 1.7d, 0 gaps >=14d), so inactivity is not the binding constraint in backtest. The binding problems are single-leg concentration and pass probability (no crypto leg clears the Tradeify bar alone, RQ-20261005-801..810). Lane scope: inventory Stage-0-pass legs on firm-tradeable symbols; register a book-level rule (max-gap, P(pass)/EV per life, daily-loss correlation) BEFORE running; run on 730d; propose a roster diff per account. It absorbs PI-20261005-MG7BGR46-0002 and files a live prop-inactivity alert as a pipeline item. The roster add is Tier-3: the manager decides it under the standing data-backed authorization, only on a committed record clearing the pre-registered rule.
